item.title: Caitlin Clark, Olivia Miles, A'ja Wilson lead 2026 First Team All-WNBA selections
item.description: Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever, WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson of the Las Vegas Aces and 2026 Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles of the Minnesota Lynx earned 2026 All-WNBA First Team selections, which the league announced ahead of Saturday's Game 3 of the WNBA Finals . Miles was the only first-timer among the First Team this season, while Clark and Fever teammate Kelsey Mitchell were named for the second time each. New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart was a First Team choice for the seventh time in her career. Atlanta Dream teammates Angel Reese and Rhyne Howard, along with Shakira Austin of the Washington Mystics were Second Team selections for the first time in their careers. 2026 All-WNBA selections First Team A'ja Wilson, Las Vegas Aces Olivia Miles, Minnesota Lynx Kelsey Mitchell, Indiana Fever Breanna Stewart, New York Liberty Caitlin Clark, Indiana Fever Wilson, who claimed her third straight WNBA MVP award this season, was named a First Team selection for the sixth time. Stewart was top 10 this season in scoring (20.8 points per game), rebounds (8.3) and blocks (1.3) while playing the fourth-most minutes (33) per night. Miles made a quick impact in her first season. The rookie of the year was a unanimous choice for the award and finished second behind Wilson in MVP voting. In 40 games, the Lynx guard averaged 19.8 points, 6 assists, 4.7 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 0.6 blocks per game while shooting 49.2% from the field and 38.8% from 3. Mitchell and Clark finished third and fourth in MVP voting. Mitchell set several WNBA regular-season records for most points (1,086), three-pointers (135), 10-plus point games (44), and 20-plus point games (35). Clark had an historic season of her own becoming the first WNBA player to finish in the top three in points (22.3 per game) and assists (8.3 per game). ATLANTA, GEORGIA - Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream reacts during the second quarter in game three of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Kevin C. Cox via Getty Images Second Team Paige Bueckers, Dallas Wings Jackie Young, Los Angeles Sparks Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream Rhyne Howard, Atlanta Dream Shakira Austin, Washington Mystics Reese, already named the Defensive Player of the Year, also led the WNBA in rebounding becoming the first player to ever grab at least 500 boards in a season (521). She also set the record for double-doubles with 32 and is just the eighth player ever to average 15-10 in a season. Howard led the WNBA in steals, ranked second in 3-pointers and was the first player ever to average at least three 3-pointers and two steals per game in a season. Austin was top-10 in MVP voting, finished fourth for Defensive Player of the Year and was five votes shy of winning Most Improved Player. She nearly averaged a double-double for the Mystics with 17 points and 9.5 rebounds per game -- making her one of three players to average 17-9 this season along with Wilson and Nneka Ogwumike. item.title: Every World Series logo since 1974: Which is your favorite?
item.description: When it comes to choosing the best or favorite World Series logo, there is rarely one definitive answer. Logo design is subjective, and every baseball fan has different reasons for preferring one logo over another. Some choose based purely on the design, while others feel a stronger connection to a particular World Series because their favorite team played in it, won it, or it was the first Fall Classic they remember watching. Pick the BEST World Series logo since 1974 ⚾️🏆 https://t.co/UqY2xyrofS — DraftKings (@DraftKings) October 22, 2026 With that in mind, here is a look at every World Series logo dating back to 1974, so baseball fans can decide which one stands out as their personal favorite. MORE: 2026 World Series will be just second of its kind in past 100 years The evolution of World Series logos Oct 22, 2026; Milwaukee, WI, USA; The Tampa Bay Rays at American Family Field during a workout session before the 2026 World Series. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images World Series logos have changed significantly over the past five decades. The designs from the 1970s and early 1980s generally featured traditional baseball imagery and straightforward typography, often incorporating the World Series name, the year, and the MLB logo. As the years progressed, the designs became more colorful and creative. The late 1980s and 1990s introduced more stylized lettering, baseball graphics, and distinctive color combinations. Some of those logos have become particularly memorable because they represented an era when MLB’s postseason branding was beginning to take on a more recognizable identity of its own. The 2000s brought another noticeable shift, with logos incorporating more three-dimensional elements, metallic effects, and increasingly elaborate graphics. Many featured baseballs, championship trophies, city imagery, or other elements designed to make each year’s World Series feel unique. More recently, MLB has moved toward cleaner and more consistent branding while still giving each World Series its own identity. The logos from the 2020s feature a mixture of modern typography, traditional baseball imagery, and references to the host cities. Looking at all of them together provides a fascinating snapshot of how baseball’s visual identity has evolved since 1974. Which World Series logo is the best? item.title: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has blamed his political opponents for hunger and poverty in Nigeria, insisting that his administration is working to address the challenges. Tinubu spoke on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign flag-off rally at Ranchers Bees Stadium, also known as Kaduna Township Stadium, in Kaduna State, ahead of the 2027 general elections. “I have an argument. I hear my opponent talking about hunger, poverty. Who created it? They did! They created the hunger, they created the poverty. We are trying to eradicate it,” the president said. He also defended his administration’s record on salary payments and commended state governors for their performance, saying they were making progress in their respective states. “We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working. I am proud of them. They are developing,” Tinubu said. The president thanked Kaduna residents for supporting him in the previous presidential election, saying their votes contributed to his emergence as president. “You gave me joy to remember the victory you gave me to become president. I come again to thank you,” he said. Tinubu appealed to Nigerians to give him another term, saying he wanted to sustain his promises of prosperity, continuity, progress and development. The post 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: “It has to be done”: Michael Carrick fires demand to his Man United stars ahead of Bournemouth
item.description: “It has to be done”: Michael Carrick fires demand to his Man United stars ahead of Bournemouth Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has made a demand of his players ahead of Sunday’s home meeting with Bournemouth. Must-win game The game against Bournemouth feels like the biggest of Carrick’s managerial career so far, given the uncertainties surrounding his position. Carrick is under immense pressure due to United’s miserable start to the season. United are languishing in the bottom half of the Premier League table, having managed just seven points from as many opening games. Wednesday’s 4-1 hammering at the hands of Como has sparked a fresh wave of criticism directed at Carrick, which was not made any easier by Bruno Fernandes questioning his tactical decisions after the final whistle. United are believed to be doing their groundwork in the event they need to pull the trigger and sack Carrick imminently. Potential replacements for the legendary midfielder include Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte, Fabian Hurzeler and Unai Emery. Carrick spoke to MUTV and demanded that his player deliver a much-improved performance when the Cherries make their way to Old Trafford. Carrick’s demand The 45-year-old said, “It has to be done. The motivation and the inspiration is there, you’ve got to feel that drive.” “We were all bitterly disappointed with a lot of things in the game [at Como] – the result, the performance.” “We’ve got a chance to put that in a different direction. We’ll never replace it, never get it back but we can make the difference in the next game now and we have to.” Carrick added, “We just want to look like ourselves, be the best version of us. We know we can be a lot better than what we were during the week.” “We are more than capable of winning football matches and we want to put the things in place to allow us to do that.” He said about Bournemouth, “They’re a very good team. I’m really impressed with them, I have to say. They are very intense and do a lot of things very, very well. They have been unfortunate with some of their results, they should have a bit more from the games, in terms of points, and I’m fully aware of what type of game it’s going to be on Sunday.” “We have to be fully ready.” The contest kicks off at 3 pm. Featured image by Molly Darlington/Getty Images

item.title: Spurs boss Ho wants 'more support and training' for WSL referees
item.description: Tottenham manager Martin Ho says Women's Super League referees "need more support" as he vented his frustration over a controversial penalty decision in their derby defeat by Arsenal. A 2-1 win for the Gunners at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday was settled by Alessia Russo's spot-kick in the 56th minute. Referee Phoebe Cross awarded the decision after Lisa Baum's shot bounced off the post and Cathinka Tandberg's clearance hit Spurs team-mate Ella Morris' outstretched hand. According to the laws, if the ball hits a hand after it was played by a team-mate, an indirect free-kick should be awarded. Ho said: "My interpretation of the rule is if your team-mate hits it and your team-mate is one yard away, time and distance is taken into account and it's not a penalty. "That's what we were told at the start of the season in the referee's meeting. I asked the question, 'how is it [a penalty] from that distance?' They couldn't give me an answer on the pitch. "I said I would come and speak to them after the game because I want to understand it, I want to understand what they're seeing. Then I can accept a decision that is there. When that decides a game, it's frustrating, because it's not within the laws of the game." Ho admitted WSL referees have "a hard enough job" to do, but believes the standards have "got worse than last year". There is currently no use of video assistant referees (VAR) or goalline technology in the WSL, while not all officials are full-time. Earlier this month, the Guardian reported the wait for full-time WSL referees was set to continue until 2029 despite a recent funding boost. Asked how standards could improve, Ho added: "They need more support and more full-time [referees]. "I understand there is probably a rule where they can't do more than one game on a weekend and that's nothing against any of the referees, but they had an elite referee [Lisa Benn] on the side the pitch. For a big game, put them in the middle. "I think that's where they need more support, more training, because when you look at most decisions that are going on, there's a lot of controversy in a lot of games. "We got two bookings in the first half but we were being dragged back by the shirt by Arsenal players and didn't get nothing. That's probably the frustrating part." BBC Sport has contacted WSL Football for a response. Tottenham still sit one point above rivals Arsenal in the WSL [Getty Images] Arsenal come from behind to beat Spurs in north London derby Arsenal relieve pressure with Spurs win - can they kick on now? item.title: Chelsea Boss Xabi Alonso Reveals More Details of Joao Pedro Injury
item.description: IMAGO / Every Second Media Chelsea v Leeds United, Carabao Cup Manager Xabi Alonso of Chelsea arrives to the stadium before the Chelsea v Leeds United Carabao Cup 3rd Round match at Stamford Bridge, London, England on 9 September 2026 Cre… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Alex Richards, LWOF Editor The squad’s dropped for Chelsea vs Tottenham Hotspur with one big absentee that shocked Blue fans. The news of a Joao Pedro injury has caused some concern after the Brazilian started hot with five goals and three assists since the start of the season. Manager Xabi Alonso spoke to the media before the London derby and provided some more details on the nature of the issue impacting the attacker. More Details on Joao Pedro Injury via Xabi Alonso Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images What The Manager Had to Say The Spaniard specified some details, noting that Pedro pulled up on Friday during training. item.title: Jacob Misiorowski Breaks Two Aroldis Chapman Records In Game 1 Of World Series
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski The Milwaukee Brewers won Game 1 of the World Series behind five strong innings from Jacob Misiorowski. He had only three strikeouts and has not been as dominant in the postseason as he was in the regular season. However, against a very tough Tampa Bay Rays lineup, he conceded just one run. As always, the velocity was noteworthy from Misiorowski. His first pitch of the game clocked in at 103.5 mph, breaking Aroldis Chapman's record for the fastest pitch thrown in a World Series game. Chapman held the record with a 103.2 mph pitch in Game 2 of the 2016 World Series. However, that was not the only record Misiorowski snatched from the current Boston Red Sox closer. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Misiorowski threw a total of 38 pitches of at least 100 mph in his Game 1 start. That broke Chapman's record of 24 pitches of at least 100 mph in Game 5 of the 2016 World Series. It took 10 years for someone to light up the radar gun like Chapman did in the World Series, but someone has finally done it. Chapman, however, is still living up to his nickname: "The Cuban Missile" He may be 38, but he can still touch triple digits. Chapman still holds the record for the fastest pitch officially recorded at 105.8 mph. Misiorowski set the record for the fastest pitch thrown by a starter earlier this year at 105.5 mph. It feels like eventually Misiorowski will surpass Chapman for the fastest pitch ever recorded, but for now, Chapman can still hold the claim to the record. More MLB: Brewers GM, Manager Offer Vague Responses When Asked About Brandon Woodruff's Role

item.title: Man City's winning start ended as Arsenal close gap to the top
item.description: (L-R) Manchester City's Erling Haaland, Marc Guehi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma during the English Premier League soccer match between Aston Villa and Manchester City at Villa Park. (is associated with: «Man City's winning start ended as Arsenal close gap to the top») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Leaders Manchester City suffered defeat for the first time in the Premier League this season after Nicolas Jackson's double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park. Unai Emery's side continued their turnaround in form after a slow start to the campaign and picked up a fourth straight win across all competitions, and their first league victory at home this season. Manchester City do not enjoy visiting Villa Park and have now lost their last four league games there, while Enzo Maresca saw his 100% league start as City boss vanish. Another tough afternoon in the west Midlands started when Marc Guehi's mistake allowed Jackson to give Villa an early lead. Villa had keeper Zion Suzuki to thank for making several vital saves, and Iliman Ndiaye crashed an effort off the post as Villa held strong to take the lead into the break. Erling Haaland grabbed his ninth league goal of the season to get City level but Jackson buried his second of the afternoon - his fourth of the season - on the hour mark to hand Villa the points. Arsenal wipe out gap to City Centre-back partners Ezri Konsa and Gabriel celebrated personal milestones as Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 to move level on points with City. England defender Konsa scrambled home from a corner in the seventh minute at the Emirates Stadium to claim his first goal for the club since arriving from Aston Villa in the summer. Gabriel sealed victory with a second-half header on his 200th Premier League appearance, ensuring the Gunners took full advantage of City's 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa in Saturday's early kick-off. Victory for Mikel Arteta's reigning champions was a seventh from eight top-flight fixtures this season and an 11th from 13 games in all competitions. Everton had opportunities to spring a surprise, with Thierno Barry and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall wasting their best openings before they slipped to a second-successive defeat. Oscar Bobb lifts Fulham out of relegation zone Oscar Bobb's first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone. Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his move from Manchester City back in January. That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa. item.title: Arsenal player ratings vs Everton: Ezri Konsa and Gabriel lead tactical masterclass in routine win
item.description: Arsenal FC v Everton - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal maintained their pursuit of the Premier League summit with a composed 2-0 victory over Everton at the Emirates Stadium. Goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel ensured Mikel Arteta's side overcame the absence of Bukayo Saka with tactical maturity. Arsenal demonstrated why they are considered one of Europe's most refined tactical machines with a professional 2-0 victory over a resilient Everton side. Despite missing the creative spark of Saka, the Gunners controlled 58% of the ball and generated an impressive 1.75 Expected Goals (xG). The breakthrough came early in the seventh minute through Konsa, setting a tone of dominance that Everton struggled to disrupt throughout the afternoon. The second half saw Arteta’s side continue to suffocate the visitors, eventually doubling their lead through Gabriel in the 68th minute. While Everton attempted to maintain a compact structure, Arsenal's 20 total shots and 12 corners reflected a relentless pressure that finally told. The victory keeps Arsenal firmly in the title hunt, showcasing their ability to find solutions through set-pieces and structured positional play when their primary individual creators are sidelined. Goalkeeper & Defence David Raya - 7/10 A largely quiet afternoon for the Spaniard, but he remained focused to make three saves and preserve the clean sheet. His distribution helped Arsenal bypass Everton's initial press, maintaining the tempo required for Arteta's system to flourish. Myles Lewis-Skelly - 7/10 The youngster showed immense tactical discipline before being replaced in the 68th minute. He managed his zone well, contributing to a defensive effort that limited Everton to just three shots on target throughout the match. Ben White - 8/10 White was instrumental in the build-up phase and provided the assist for Gabriel's crucial second goal in the 68th minute. His overlapping runs and technical security were vital in a game where Arsenal lacked their usual width on the right. Gabriel - 9/10 An elite performance from the Brazilian, who combined defensive solidity with a clinical edge. He scored the decisive second goal in the 68th minute and was the primary reason Arsenal won six air challenges while losing only two. Ezri Konsa - 8/10 Operating in a slightly adjusted role, Konsa provided the perfect start by scoring the opening goal in just the seventh minute. His reading of the game prevented Everton from developing any meaningful counter-attacks. Midfield Martin Oedegaard - 8/10 The captain was the conductor of the orchestra, constantly probing the Everton low block. Midfield Martin Oedegaard - 8/10 The captain was the conductor of the orchestra, constantly probing the Everton low block. While he didn't register a goal involvement, his movement between the lines opened the spaces that led to Arsenal's 12 corners. Declan Rice - 7/10 A typically industrious performance in the engine room. Rice covered significant ground to ensure Arsenal were never exposed on the transition, recording a high volume of successful interceptions before his 80th-minute withdrawal. Mikel Merino - 7/10 Merino provided the physical presence needed to combat Everton's midfield. His ability to win second balls and progress play vertically was essential during the first hour of the contest. Attack Eberechi Eze - 7/10 Stepping into a creative role, Eze showed flashes of brilliance. While he found it difficult to break through a crowded penalty area, his presence forced Everton to double-team him, creating room for others. Noni Madueke - 6/10 Madueke worked hard on the flank but often lacked the final ball to unlock the Toffees' defence. He contributed to the 20 shots Arsenal took but will be disappointed not to have tested Pickford more frequently. Viktor Gyoekeres - 8/10 The striker was a constant nuisance for the Everton centre-backs. He provided the assist for Konsa's early opener and his relentless pressing set the defensive line high for the Gunners. Substitutes & Manager Kai Havertz - 6/10 Introduced in the 68th minute to provide a different aerial threat and tactical flexibility as Arsenal looked to see out the result. Bruno Guimaraes - 6/10 Brought on for the final 22 minutes to provide fresh legs and ball retention in the middle of the park. Riccardo Calafiori - 6/10 Replaced Lewis-Skelly to solidify the left flank and ensured no late drama occurred near the Arsenal box. Max Dowman - N/A A late introduction in the 80th minute, not enough time to significantly impact the flow of the game. Martín Zubimendi - N/A Came on in the 80th minute to shore up the midfield and help see out the 2-0 victory. Mikel Arteta - 9/10 Arteta managed the game perfectly despite receiving a yellow card in the 64th minute. His decision to rely on set-piece structures and high-volume crossing (27 total) paid off, and his quadruple substitution in the 68th minute effectively killed the game's momentum for Everton.

item.title: Maresca backs Man City defender after first Premier League defeat of season
item.description: Maresca backs Man City defender after first Premier League defeat of season Enzo Maresca insists he has no concerns over Marc Guehi after substituting the defender during Manchester City’s 2-1 defeat to Aston Villa. Guehi was taken off at the break having made an error for Villa’s opener and also been booked in the first half. But Maresca has backed the defender and insists he is not concerned by his performance. “It’s just a technical decision, like it happens in all the games that the manager decides to make a change,” Maresca said. “I’m not worried about Marc at all. I know that he is playing every minute since the season started with us and with the international team. “It’s not easy but the change was also because he had a yellow card, and the way we want to be aggressive sometimes, to have one yellow card can be dangerous. “But I’m not worried at all.” Maresca also felt City deserved more from the game at Villa Park. “I think we deserved more from the game, for the amount of chances that we created and for the chances that we conceded,” he said.

item.title: 1 assist, 2 key passes: Jayce Fitzgerald continues to be Man United’s shining light on loan
item.description: 1 assist, 2 key passes: Jayce Fitzgerald continues to be Man United’s shining light on loan Manchester United had only one player involved in loan action this Saturday afternoon. Loan situation Injuries to Jack Moorhouse and Dan Gore have derailed their loan progress. Sekou Kone and Jacob Devaney were both gaining substantial minutes, but direct red cards have seen them suspended recently. Chido Obi has also seen his game time limited to minutes off the bench, and Altay Bayindir is yet to play for Celta Vigo. Therefore, alongside Andre Onana, Jayce Fitzgerald has been the United loanee who has been involved the most for his loan side. Match vs Shrewsbury Town Fitzgerald played the entire match as his Rotherham United side played out an entertaining 3-3 draw with Shrewsbury Town. The game was also noteworthy for United fans as former player Brandon Williams came off the bench for the final 30 minutes of the game. Fitzgerald’s biggest contribution was an assist to Tom Bradshaw as the Millers equalised 2-2 despite playing with a man less. The 19-year-old’s ball was described as “perfect” by Rotherham’s social media as he continues to impress for the League Two side. The United midfielder made two key passes in the match and completed two crosses for the home side. He also made 74% of his passes and had one shot on goal. Fitzgerald could not complete any dribbles or tackles for his side. The United man made two clearances, but he could not win any duels as he was outmuscled in the centre of the park. He will next be in action away to Swindon Town on Halloween afternoon. Jayce Fitzgerald stats vs Shrewsbury Town Feature image Matt McNulty via Getty Images online polls

item.title: BYU, Tennessee and Texas face dangerous matchups after Week 7
item.description: Source: C5Media/Depositphotos Week 7 of the 2026 college football season delivered a reminder that strong records offer little protection against an unpredictable Saturday. BYU climbed to No. 2 nationally, Tennessee defeated Alabama, and Texas suffered another damaging loss after Florida rallied in Austin. Those results leave all 3 programs facing important tests as the season moves deeper into conference play. BYU must protect its undefeated record against UCF, Tennessee travels to South Carolina after its statement victory, and Texas welcomes a dangerous Ole Miss team with its postseason hopes under pressure. Each matchup presents a different challenge. BYU faces the difficulty of sustaining its rise, Tennessee must prove its breakthrough was not a one-week achievement, and Texas needs a response after consecutive setbacks threatened to derail its season. BYU must handle the pressure of its new ranking BYU moved to No. 2 in the Associated Press Top 25 after defeating previously undefeated Notre Dame 28-24. The Cougars improved to 6-0, earned a signature victory, and strengthened their position in the national championship conversation. The challenge now is maintaining that momentum. Higher rankings bring greater expectations, and opponents have additional motivation when facing an undefeated team. BYU cannot afford to treat its next opponent as a routine assignment simply because its own record looks impressive. The Cougars visit UCF on Saturday, Oct. 24, for a Big 12 matchup in Orlando. Playing away from home adds another complication, particularly after the emotional and physical demands of beating Notre Dame in a nationally significant contest. UCF has an opportunity to disrupt BYU’s momentum UCF represents a different challenge from Notre Dame. The Knights will have home-field advantage and an opportunity to test a BYU team that has spent recent weeks climbing the national rankings while navigating a demanding schedule. For BYU, the priority will be to avoid costly mistakes and maintain offensive consistency. A strong start could quiet the home crowd, while turnovers or missed opportunities could allow UCF to stay competitive and turn the game into a late contest. The Cougars also need to remain disciplined defensively. Their undefeated record has put them among the teams receiving serious national attention, but another road opponent can exploit lapses that might have been overlooked during earlier victories. South Carolina has the opportunity to challenge Tennessee’s rhythm, making this a useful test of whether the Volunteers can turn a statement victory into sustained progress. Texas needs an immediate response after another loss Texas entered the season with high expectations, but its latest results have raised difficult questions. The Longhorns lost 27-24 to Florida in Week 7, falling to 4-2 after previously losing to Oklahoma by the same score. The defeat against Florida was especially damaging because it came at home against an unranked opponent. Texas had built a 14-point lead but could not hold it, allowing the Gators to leave Austin with a victory that reshaped the Longhorns’ season. Texas dropped from No. 7 to No. 19 in the AP poll following the loss. That fall reflects the cost of consecutive defeats, but the remaining schedule still offers opportunities to recover if the team can correct its mistakes and produce a more complete performance. Ole Miss presents another major test for Texas Texas hosts Ole Miss on Saturday, Oct. 24, in a matchup with significant consequences for both teams. The Rebels entered Week 8 ranked No. 7 nationally with a 5-1 record, giving the Longhorns a chance to regain credibility against a highly ranked opponent. The biggest concern for Texas is consistency. The Longhorns have shown they can compete with quality teams, but losing consecutive games by identical scores suggests that small mistakes and missed opportunities are becoming costly. They need to finish drives and protect leads more effectively. Ole Miss, meanwhile, has a chance to take advantage of Texas’ recent struggles. A victory in Austin would strengthen the Rebels’ position in the SEC race and deepen the pressure on the Longhorns. Texas must make better decisions in key moments to avoid another damaging result. Source: EyepixGroup/Depositphotos Week 8 could reshape the national picture The three matchups carry different stakes, but each could influence how the teams are viewed heading into the second half of the season. BYU is protecting an undefeated record, Tennessee is trying to build on its win over Alabama, and Texas is attempting to stop its slide. For BYU, a road victory would reinforce its place near the top of the rankings. Tennessee could demonstrate that its defensive performance against Alabama was sustainable, while Texas needs a win over Ole Miss to restore confidence and remain relevant in the national conversation. The outcomes will not decide every postseason possibility, but they could change the direction of each team’s season. With the College Football Playoff picture still developing, Week 8 offers all 3 programs an important opportunity to strengthen their cases or expose unresolved weaknesses. What each team must do to avoid an upset BYU’s path begins with discipline. The Cougars need to handle the road environment, protect the ball in possession, and avoid giving UCF easy scoring opportunities. Their ranking makes them a target, and a focused performance matters more than the attention surrounding their rise. Tennessee must show that its victory over Alabama was the product of repeatable strengths. The Volunteers need to carry their defensive intensity to South Carolina while maintaining enough offensive balance to prevent the game from becoming a struggle for field position. Texas faces the most urgent need for a reset. The Longhorns must convert scoring chances, defend leads, and reduce late-game errors against Ole Miss. A victory would provide a meaningful response to consecutive losses, while another defeat would intensify questions about the team’s ability to meet its preseason expectations. item.title: EPL: Arsenal see off Everton, go joint-top after Man City defeat
item.description: Manchester City’s flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. Nicolas Jackson struck twice for Unai Emery’s men to continue a fine run of form for a new-look Villa side. Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half, but Maresca was left to rue City not making more of their dominance for large spells of the game. “We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box,” said Maresca. The Villa side that won the Europa League last season was decimated by high-profile departures during the transfer window. But Emery has quickly moulded his new squad into shape with Jackson proving his critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea wrong. The Senegal international pounced on an error by Marc Guehi to fire Villa ahead after just six minutes. Another of Villa’s new signings Zion Suzuki then thwarted City with a string of stunning saves. Haaland headed in his 13th goal in 10 games this season to equalise. Villa, though, swiftly responded as Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep out Jackson’s low shot on the hour mark. “A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park,” said Emery. “We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic.” – Arsenal’s set-piece prowess – Arsenal took advantage to move alongside City on 21 points from eight games with a routine 2-0 win against Everton. Shorn of the creative inspiration of Bukayo Saka, who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Arsenal had to rely on their set-piece prowess to get the job done. Ezri Konsa bundled in his first goal for the club after Everton failed to clear a corner to open the scoring on seven minutes. Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the lead for Mikel Arteta’s men midway through the second period. Fulham further eased the pressure on manager Alvaro Arbeloa with a 1-0 win at Coventry thanks to Oscar Bobb’s individual effort. A second consecutive victory propels the Cottagers out of the relegation zone and up to 12th. Tottenham are also seeking to escape the bottom three when they travel to Chelsea in the evening kick-off, aiming to improve on a terrible record at Stamford Bridge. On Sunday the focus turns on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick when his side take on Bournemouth. A seven-game winless streak has plunged Carrick’s future into doubt just months after he was hired on a two-year deal after a successful interim spell in charge at the end of last season. AFP The post EPL: Arsenal see off Everton, go joint-top after Man City defeat appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Chelsea v Tottenham: Premier League – live
item.description: ⚽ Premier League updates from the 5.30pm BST kick-off ⚽ Aston Villa 2-1 Man City | Live scores | Table | Mail Scott The teams take to the pitch. Chelsea in blue, Spurs in white, and it won’t be long before every shirt is soaking wet. Has the signature work of the Harry J All Stars ever been so apposite? We’ll be off in a couple of minutes. Roberto De Zerbi also speaks to Sky. “James Maddison is a very important player … he brings personality, qualities, experience … a different position on the pitch … he’s a different player to Conor Gallagher or [Omar] Marmoush as a number ten … we have to find him in the right moment in the best position … [Dominic Solanke] felt fatigue after Coventry … I am lucky to have a big squad with many different solutions … so I took the decision [to rest him] but the game is 90 minutes.” Continue reading...

item.title: Fulham snatch late winner at relegation rivals Coventry to emerge from bottom three
item.description: Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone. Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27m move from Manchester City back in January. That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa. Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard ’s side second-bottom of the table. Coventry’s Brandon Thomas-Asante and Fulham’s Antonee Robinson battle for the ball (Mike Egerton/PA). The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing. Quality was in short supply between two sides who started the day in the bottom three. King should have broken the deadlock in the 18th minute when afforded too much space in the box, but his powerful strike rebounded off the top of the upright before Alex Iwobi sent a wild follow-up effort high and wide. At the other end, Bobby Thomas met Rudoni’s free-kick but got his angles all wrong as he headed well wide, before Brandon Thomas-Asante headed wide from Jay Dasilva’s cross following a good run forward from Rudoni. A mis-hit backpass from Antonee Robinson offered Thomas-Asante another chance but his shot lacked power as Leno easily gathered. While Coventry were piling up half-chances Fulham were the ones bossing possession but, in keeping with their season so far, struggling to turn that sort of dominance into goals. Coventry defender Milan van Ewijk almost helped them out, deflecting Robinson’s low cross dangerously close to his own goal as it found the side-netting. Just before the break, Calvin Bassey went down in the box claiming a shirt-pull from Thomas-Asante, but referee Adam Herczeg waved play on with replays suggesting they each had a hold of the other. VAR had taken a look, and was involved again early in the second half when Rudoni’s free-kick from the right struck Iwobi on the arm before he cleared, but the Nigerian’s arms were by his side and play was waved on. Coventry then suffered a major blow when the in-form Thomas, praised by Frank Lampard in midweek, hobbled off just before the hour, replaced by teenage Manchester City loanee Stephen Mfuni. The hosts were starting to build some momentum after a series of substitutions but it swiftly ended as Bobb struck with 10 minutes to go. Oscar Bobb scored a late winner at Coventry (Getty) Coventry tried to respond but a powerful strike from Matt Grimes

item.title: Gabriel Gets 8.5, Konsa With 8 | Arsenal Players Rated In Solid Win Vs Everton
item.description: Gabriel Gets 8.5, Konsa With 8 | Arsenal Players Rated In Solid Win Vs Everton Arsenal entertained Everton at the Emirates Stadium earlier today as they looked to secure a positive result at home in the Premier League. The Gunners made a bright start to the game and took the lead in the seventh minute when Ezri Konsa found the back of the net. Mikel Arteta’s men went into the half-time break 1-0 up on the scoreline. Gabriel doubled his side’s advantage in the 68th minute as the Gunners earned a solid 2-0 win in front of their home fans. Let’s take a look at how each Arsenal player fared during the clash against the Toffees. He made a few decent saves during the game and deserves credit for keeping a clean sheet. RB: Ben White – 7/10 White cleared his lines when he could and engineered a few inviting chances going forward. CB: Ezri Konsa – 8/10 He performed his defensive duties well and managed to score the opener in the seventh minute. CB: Gabriel – 8.5/10 Gabriel gave a good account of himself on the defensive end of the field and was tidy with his passing. He managed to double his side’s advantage in the 68th minute. LONDON, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 24: Gabriel of Arsenal scores his team’s second goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Arsenal FC and Everton at Emirates Stadium on October 24, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) LB: Myles Lewis-Skelly – 7/10 He caught the eye at times on both halves. CM: Declan Rice – 7.5/10 Rice earned possession back twice and engineered a few promising chances for his teammates to score. CM: Mikel Merino – 6.5/10 He was not shy of having a strike at goal and was replaced in the 67th minute. RW: Noni Madueke – 6.5/10 Madueke caused a few problems for his marker, but there was no goal for him. CAM: Martin Odegaard – 7/10 He was a real menace up top but failed to register a goal. LW: Eberechi Eze – 6.5/10 Eze managed to shine at times on the left flank and was substituted in the 79th minute. ST: Viktor Gyokeres – 7/10 He engineered a few impressive chances for others around him and has an assist to show for his efforts. ST: Kai Havertz – 6/10 His impact on the game was minimal. CM: Bruno Guimaraes – 6.5/10 Guimaraes made one key chance in the final third. LB: Riccardo Calafiori – 6.5/10 He was solid at the back. CM: Martin Zubimendi – 6/10 Zubimendi added some energy to Arteta’s midfield. He made one good run with the ball.

item.title: Bayern Munich without three key players for Freiburg clash
item.description: Bayern Munich without three key players for Freiburg clash Bayern Munich will be looking to maintain their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season when they travel to Europa-Park Stadion to face Freiburg. The Bavarian giants sit top of the Bundesliga table with 14 points from six games and have already scored 22 goals. Freiburg have impressed this season, too, sitting third in the table with 13 points after picking up four wins. Bayern Munich injury news vs Freiburg (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) Bayern are dealing with several injury and fitness concerns ahead of the match. Christian Falk has informed CFBayern Insider that Manuel Neuer will not be available for Bayern’s away Bundesliga fixture against Freiburg. The Bayern skipper will sit out the match due to persistent tendon irritation in his foot. Falk said: “His foot appears to remain a weak point for Manuel Neuer; we recall that he previously suffered a serious foot injury. “This makes it all the more important to have a successor like Jonas Urbig already within the club’s ranks. We have heard that he was promised 25 competitive appearances this season as part of a transition period—a number that could now even increase, given the issues with Neuer’s foot.” The Bavarian giants could also be without Vincent Kompany in the dugout for this game. Kompany required medical attention on Friday after collapsing during a training session involving Bayern’s reserve team. The first-team head coach had been observing the second team’s session when the incident occurred. Kompany is currently undergoing a thorough examination in hospital and will remain under medical care, with his coaching staff overseeing all training and match-related operations in the meantime. Luis Diaz also picked up an injury during Bayern’s 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League and is expected to be out for at least a few weeks. Bayern will also be without their influential midfielder Joshua Kimmich, who has been granted compassionate leave following the death of his father. Kimmich has yet to return to Bayern training. Bayern Munich: Tough game vs Freiburg (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) Jonas Urbig is a highly talented goalkeeper, and Bayern have full confidence in his abilities, believing he has the potential to become the club’s first-choice goalkeeper in the future. Urbig is likely to start in goal, while Tom Bischof should feature in midfield alongside Aleksandar Pavlovic. Bayern have drawn two away games this season, and Freiburg could pose a stern test given their impressive form.

item.title: Jaguars get Brian Thomas Jr. trade update from NFL execs that's not a surprise
item.description: Jaguars get Brian Thomas Jr. trade update from NFL execs that's not a surprise originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars are heading into their Week 7 bye with a lot of eyes on them. While the Jaguars lead the AFC South, the attention is not due to how good the team is, but rather to a potential trade. After not playing a single snap in the second-half of Week 6, Brian Thomas Jr., the Jaguars first-round wide receiver from the 2024 NFL Draft, seems like a very reasonable trade candidate. Jacksonville hasn't made their plans known, but ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Saturday morning that multiple NFL executives believe the Jaguars will "seriously consider" a trade of Thomas, which shouldn't come as a surprise at all. Jaguars reportedly will 'seriously consider' trading Brian Thomas Jr. "Multiple league execs believe Jacksonville will seriously consider trading Brian Thomas Jr. at the deadline now that his role has decreased," Fowler reports. This is not a surprise at all for the Jaguars, as all of the signs this season, and even over the NFL offseason, pointed to Thomas being a trade chip. Parker Washington has completely broken out as a No. 1 wide receiver, and Jakobi Meyers is a very strong No. 2 option in Liam Coen's offense. Josh Cameron has played himself into a bigger role, and with Travis Hunter able to get onto the field and make a meaningful impact as a WR, the Jaguars don't really have a need for Thomas. MORE : Travis Hunter made NFL history, but the Jaguars still left London with a loss While trading him might require the team to explore some WR depth options, the potential return for a trade of the first-rounder might be appealing enough to move the needle for Jacksonville. Will they actually trade him? It's not impossible, especially if there's a team willing to take a chance on Thomas as a long-term option. The Las Vegas Raiders make a ton of sense, as do a team like the New York Giants . This is a trade situation to closely monitor, as all indications are that a deal is very much under consideration for the Jaguars. It's not locked in like the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade was, but Thomas is a name to keep a very close eye on going forward this year. More NFL news: Why Colts are likely sellers after firing Chris Ballard before NFL trade deadline Aaron Rodgers blasts Buccaneers' field as 'one of the worst surfaces in the league' Cam Skattebo's lack of rushing attempts is a major cause for concern for Giants ESPN analyst believes Browns are a quarterback away from being Super Bowl contenders ESPN analyst proposes Eagles trade Saquon Barkley to Texans for very intriguing haul

item.title: Steelers Give Aaron Rodgers Another Familiar Option
item.description: receiver Brandon Smith at training camp on Aug. 7, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now For the third week in a row, the Pittsburgh Steelers have elevated Brandon Smith from the practice squad. Smith , who has a prior rapport with quarterback Aaron Rodgers, has played 57 offensive snaps this season, including 41 during last Sunday’s win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Steelers had signed Smith to a reserve/future contract at the end of last season. He had stints with the Jets during the 2024 and 2025 seasons, spending time on both the active roster and practice squad. Smith has also made stops with the New England Patriots, Dallas Cowboys and Arizona Cardinals. “He cooked a lot of guys in the (practice) squad. I mean, every single day, B-Smith was making plays,” Rodgers said earlier this month of Smith’s time with the Jets. “I think he really transformed his body too. Lost a little bit of weight, got a little faster. He’s a smart guy. He’s quiet, goes about his business, very professional. Very, very good in practice. Shows a lot of things. “I have a lot of trust in him. Knows the plan every week even when he’s been down, and so I expect B-Smith to be able to step in and play as well as he possibly can.” Related Headlines Steelers Add Experienced Wide Receiver for Saints Game Steelers to Debut New Uniform Combination in Paris Future Steelers Opponent Loses Starter For Season Read more at Steelers Now

The Green Bay Packers have become an intriguing team to watch ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, with speculation linking them to Arizona Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat . This potential move has an unusual connection to the Micah Parsons trade, as Dallas is also being mentioned as a possible destination for Sweat while Green Bay awaits Parsons’ return from a knee injury. Additionally, the Packers are facing another defensive setback ahead of Sunday’s NFC North matchup against Detroit. Linebacker Zaire Franklin has been ruled out due to a shin injury sustained during practice , joining Edgerrin Cooper on the list of unavailable starters. Fortunately, head coach Matt LaFleur does not expect Franklin’s absence to require a stint on injured reserve. Currently at 4-2, Green Bay has valid reasons to explore reinforcements for a roster that has successfully navigated significant injuries while winning three consecutive games. General manager Brian Gutekunst has already made several personnel changes, and the upcoming deadline could provide an opportunity to recover valuable resources from an offensive position where responsibilities have become increasingly concentrated. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Veteran tight end Jonnu Smith is the player the Packers should consider trading before November 10, provided another team is willing to offer meaningful compensation for his experience. Jonnu Smith’s limited involvement creates an interesting decision Ed Mulholland-Imagn Images Smith arrived in Green Bay shortly before the regular season, signing a one-year contract in August after spending the previous season with the Pittsburgh Steelers. His addition made sense at the time, especially since Tucker Kraft was recovering from a serious knee injury and Luke Musgrave was unavailable due to a neck issue. The Packers were looking for another experienced receiving option who could contribute from various alignments. Smith brought that experience, having earned Pro Bowl recognition with Miami in 2024 after recording 88 receptions for 884 yards and eight touchdowns. His ability to work from the slot, backfield, and traditional tight end positions provided head coach Matt LaFleur with a versatile option while Green Bay assessed the health of its established contributors, but in the first six games, Smith’s role has been considerably smaller than expected. He has appeared in four games, catching five passes for 85 yards but has yet to score a touchdown. His most notable performance was in the season opener against Minnesota, where he made two receptions for 50 yards, including a 43-yard gain. Since that game, Smith’s opportunities have diminished as Kraft has established himself as the primary receiving threat at the tight end position. Additionally, Green Bay’s offense has become more comfortable integrating its younger wide receivers, particularly Matthew Golden, whose development has provided quarterback Jordan Love with another reliable option. The Packers have benefited from these adjustments, winning three consecutive games and showing greater offensive consistency after a challenging start to the season. Although Smith remains capable of contributing when needed, the gap between his previous production and his current role raises a reasonable opportunity for general manager Brian Gutekunst to evaluate the trade market. An organization facing tight end injuries might find his receiving experience valuable, especially if it requires someone who can operate in multiple formations. While moving Smith would sacrifice useful depth, the potential return could be worth considering while he still has a recognizable résumé and an expiring contract. Tucker Kraft has become the foundation of Green Bay’s tight end rotation Barry Reeger-Imagn Images The Packers’ decision will ultimately depend on the level of confidence they have in the depth behind Kraft. The fourth-year tight end has returned from his knee injury in 2025 and has resumed a central role in LaFleur’s offense, providing Love with a reliable target through the middle of the field. Kraft’s development has allowed Green Bay to create favorable passing opportunities without spreading significant receiving responsibilities among multiple tight ends. This focus has reduced the immediate importance of Smith’s receiving ability, even though the veteran continues to offer valuable experience that would be difficult to replace with an inexperienced backup. Mark Redman has also provided another option since he arrived from the Los Angeles Rams in an August trade. Green Bay acquired him for a 2028 seventh-round selection, valuing his physical blocking ability and willingness to take on traditional in-line assignments. Additionally, Josh Whyle remains on the roster, giving the coaching staff more personnel options for formations that require multiple tight ends. These players each bring different qualities, allowing LaFleur to design offensive packages tailored to specific assignments while Kraft handles a significant portion of the passing game responsibilities. Musgrave’s ongoing absence complicates the situation, as Green Bay cannot assume that another tight end will be available immediately if needed. The organization will need to assess Musgrave’s recovery and evaluate whether the remaining healthy players can take on Smith’s responsibilities before making any decisions. Trading an experienced backup during a playoff race carries additional risks, especially when the starter has recently returned from a major injury. Therefore, Gutekunst should set a meaningful asking price instead of trading Smith just because his receiving statistics have declined. The Packers invested in him as insurance against injuries, and that insurance remains valuable as the schedule becomes more demanding. A trade may become appealing if another team is willing to offer compensation that outweighs the potential challenges Green Bay could face if Kraft suffers further setbacks. Green Bay could turn veteran depth into resources for its defense The strongest argument for exploring a trade involving Za’Darius Smith arises from the injuries currently impacting Green Bay’s defensive lineup. Cooper’s Achilles injury has sidelined one of the Packers’ most promising linebackers for the rest of the season, while Franklin’s unexpected absence adds to the challenges they face against Detroit. Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper are expected to take on larger roles, with Nick Niemann also available to contribute. This situation could accelerate the development of Green Bay’s younger defenders, but relying on an inexperienced rotation becomes increasingly difficult when facing opponents with strong rushing attacks and versatile receiving threats. Detroit poses exactly such a challenge, with Jahmyr Gibbs capable of contributing both as a runner and a receiver. Additionally, the Packers have experienced significant injuries along the defensive line, including the loss of Javon Hargrave to an Achilles injury. These absences heighten the urgency of identifying reliable contributors who can handle various assignments within Jonathan Gannon’s defensive scheme. Green Bay has already been linked to potential pass-rushing acquisitions, including Sweat, whose previous experience with Gannon makes the possibility intriguing. The eventual return of Parsons would also greatly enhance the defense, but his rehabilitation process must be carefully considered when assessing the additional help the defense might need. Acquiring valuable draft compensation for Smith could improve Green Bay’s flexibility in trade discussions. item.title: Three things we learnt from Bundesliga Matchday 7 – Antonio Nusa, Werder Bremen are fun and Said El Mala
item.description: Three things we learnt from Bundesliga Matchday 7 – Antonio Nusa, Werder Bremen are fun and Said El Mala Borussia Mönchengladbach began Bundesliga Matchday 7 with a 3-2 win against Stuttgart to avoid setting an all-time Bundesliga record for the worst start ever. Saturday afternoon was a day for the mid-table teams, with Augsburg playing Union Berlin, Köln hosting Schalke, Mainz facing Werder Bremen, Paderborn against Hamburg and RB Leipzig versus Elversberg. Here are the three things we learnt: Antonio Nusa is RB Leipzig’s most important player: In the summer, Nusa was an important player for Norway’s run to the quarter-finals of the World Cup, and he has seemingly carried on this form into this season. In seven Bundesliga games, the winger has three goals and five assists, which makes him the RB Leipzig player with the most goal involvements in the league, ahead of Christopher Nkunku. With the Frenchman out for the game against Elversberg, Nusa stepped up again, providing two assists as Martin Demichelis’ side beat newly promoted Elversberg 4-0 at home. If Nusa continues this form, he will likely be Leipzig’s next big sale in the summer. However, in his two full seasons at the Red Bull Arena, the 21-year-old’s main problem has been staying injury-free, as he has hit similar veins of form only for injury to derail him, and he cannot find the same form when he returns. Werder Bremen are a fun team: After they struggled in the Bundesliga last season, Werder Bremen have turned themselves into a team where their games may be must-watch, mainly due to the goals involved. In their past five games, they’ve had three comebacks and scored five, four, four, and today five goals after beating Mainz 3-2. Niclas Füllkrug again pitched in with a double from the penalty spot before Anthony Caci made it 2-1 just before the break. In the second half, Ludovic Reis made it 3-1, but two minutes later Jae-Sung Lee made it 3-2, and unlike their opponents in the past few weeks, Bremen were able to hold on to secure the three points and move into sixth. Obviously, this is entirely unsustainable, and if Bremen are going to be outsiders for a European spot this season, they need to shore up their defence. Said El Mala should have been sent off: After a transfer saga in the summer, and what seemed like a hot start to the season, Said El Mala’s Bundesliga campaign has stalled in recent weeks. The 20-year-old has largely been ineffective for Köln, and that was shown today in their 0-0 draw with Schalke. However, an argument can be made that El Mala shouldn’t have even been on the pitch for the 80 minutes he was. There was a moment just before half-time where El Mala pushed Schalke’s Soufian El-Faouzi into Robin Gosens as both were challenging for an aerial ball. This resulted in the pair colliding head-on and ultimately both being substituted off. El Mala was punished in no way at all, not even a yellow card. GGFN | Jack Meenan

item.title: Namibia beat Ireland after Erasmus' 156 not out
item.description: Gerhard Erasmus previous highest ODI score had been 125 [Getty Images] Second one-day international, Windhoek Namibia 321-6 (50 overs): Erasmus 156* (125), Frylinck 76 (90); Hoey 3-53 Ireland 290 (47.3 overs): Stirling 77 (71); Brassell 4-52 Namibia win by 31 runs, five-game series tied 1-1 Scorecard An unbeaten 156 from Gerhard Erasmus saw Namibia level their five-game one-day international series against Ireland at one win apiece. The Namibia captain twice took the game away from the tourists in Windhoek as his side won by 31 runs. First, a career-best effort with the bat helped set an imposing total of 32. The 31-year-old then took the final two wickets of the game as Ireland's tail threatened to make an unlikely chase. Ireland captain Paul Stirling won the toss and, having put the hosts into bat, saw his bowling attack struggle, especially in the death overs. Again without leading seamer Mark Adair, Byron McDonough took a wicket with the first ball of his spell but ended up with 1-71. Curtis Campher's 10 innings were also costly as he finished with 1-74. Spinner Gavin Hoey was the pick of the bunch as he matched his trio of wickets from Wednesday's victory, this time with figures of 3-53. As they set about chasing 322, Stirling's uptick in form continued with a second half-century of the series, this time with a knock of 77 from 71 deliveries. His wicket, leg before off the bowling of Jack Brassell, however ended a spell where three batters were dismissed for the addition of just six runs. Brassell was the pick of Namibia bowlers, accounting for not only Stirling but also Lorcan Tucker, George Dockrell and Curtis Campher as he finished with 4-52. A ninth-wicket stand of 58 from Hoey and Jai Moondra briefly brought Ireland within sight, but when the latter was out for 20, caught and bowled by Erasmus, hopes were quickly dashed. The series resumes on Tuesday in Windhoek as Ireland continue their preparations for next year's World Cup qualifiers.

item.title: Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby
item.description: Freddie Steward points at Henry Pollock, who is busy exchanging words with Ollie Chessum as tensions boil over at half-time Leicester came from behind to win a feisty East Midlands derby with a second-half power play that took the Tigers into second place in the Prem. Northampton led 7-3 at half-time after a seventh-minute try by teenage full-back James Pater but Leicester’s pack turned up the heat on the champions with three tries in 13 minutes after the break. Henry Pollock, who was replaced in the 52nd minute, was at the centre of a mass flare-up that carried on into the tunnel as tempers boiled over at the end of the first half. It's all HEATING up as we reach half-time in the East Midlands derby 😤🔥Henry Pollock is right in the thick of things 👀📺 Stream TNT Sports on HBO Maxhttps://t.co/ISqfkeU3vl https://t.co/QOz1TqjjED — Rugby on TNT Sports (@rugbyontnt) October 24, 2026 The incident served to spark a second-half onslaught by the home side at Mattioli Woods Welford Road. A catch-and-drive score from hooker Jamie Blamire was followed by a fine try in the left-hand corner by second row Cam Henderson, after a huge Tigers scrum, and a close-range touchdown from flanker Finn Carnduff. With Northampton down to 14 men after replacement Tom Lockett was sin-binned for a high tackle on Solomone Kata, Freddie Steward went over for the bonus-point try eight minutes from time. On a chastening afternoon for the Saints, they also had to withdraw England stand-off Fin Smith late on after he had carried a leg injury for an hour of the game. Saints are powerless to influence things and Searle boots it out of play to the roars of a sold-out Welford Road. The Tigers take home the bragging rights! It was a stodgy first half from both teams - but Leicester were arguably second best with their faltering lineout. Who would have thought they needed a good old half-time scuffle to refocus them? It is a route one kind of a day. But it probably does not do Pollock any favours in terms of pushing his case as a man for all seasons. The TMO has spotted a high hit from replacement lock Tom Lockett on Hamer-Webb in the build up to all of that.. and after a lengthy look Radwan’s yellow card is reversed and instead dished out to Lockett. item.title: Como follow Man Utd thumping with victory in Serie A
item.description: Como backed up their brilliant Champions League victory over Manchester United as Anastasios Douvikas scored twice in a 2-0 Serie A win against Sassuolo on Saturday. Cesc Fabregas’s side climbed to fourth in the table, just two points adrift of early leaders Inter Milan who host Fiorentina on Sunday. Como were frustrated for long periods by a stubborn Sassuolo team, but clinched an ultimately comfortable win courtesy of Douvikas’s two goals in the space of 11 second-half minutes. The Greece striker has now scored five goals in his last four games, and eight in all competitions in total this season. Como, who qualified for Europe for the first time in their history last term, thrashed Man United 4-1 in the Champions League in midweek. Later Saturday, Roma bid to go top of the table when they visit Napoli, before second-placed Lazio also eye the summit in their home game against Parma. AFP The post Como follow Man Utd thumping with victory in Serie A appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Millennium stays perfect with overtime win against Canyon View
item.description: Millennium remained unbeaten, defeating Canyon View, 6-3, in overtime on Friday, Oct. 23, in a game that was scoreless after four quarters. Millennium (No. 5 in AIA/MaxPreps 5A rankings) moved to 9-0 and Canyon View (No. 10) dropped to 7-2. Key plays Canyon View scored first in overtime on an Austin Honsa field goal. Millennium answered on a Kadin Johnson touchdown to win the game. Key players Millennium quarterback Myron Lee, who threw the winning TD pass. "I got kind of down on myself, in my head and the team just came and picked me up," Lee said when asked how he kept his mind straight through the game. Austin Honsa, who got Canyon View on the board in overtime. Kadin Johnson, who caught the winning TD pass for Millennium. Quotes "They're undefeated for a reason, we know they are one of the top teams in the state." — Canyon View coach Manuel Alcantar "They have been built for this, we have 38 seniors and they have been through a lot, being there for each other" — Millennium coach Lamar Early Upcoming Millenium plays its final regular-season game on Friday, Oct. 30 against Goodyear rival Desert Edge. Canyon View plays its regular-season finale against Tolleson on Thursday, Oct. 29. This article originally appeared on Arizona Republic: Millennium stays perfect with overtime win against Canyon View

item.title: Scarlets denied by Stormers in 14-try thriller
item.description: Scarlets centre Joe Roberts made his Wales debut in 2023 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] United Rugby Championship Stormers (33) 52 Tries: Porthen, Pead, Mchunu, Senatla, Fourie, Reid, Ahmed 2 Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu 6 Scarlets (14) 40 Tries: Roberts 3, Jones, Page, Macleod Cons: Leggatt-Jones 5 Centre Joe Roberts scored a hat-trick, but Scarlets suffered defeat by Stormers in a remarkable 14-try United Rugby Championship (URC) contest. A late double by Yaqeen Ahmed sealed victory for the South Africans, with the Llanelli-based side having to be content with a try bonus when they had given themselves a shot at a famous win. While the UK was battered by Storm Boelo and south west Wales was still suffering the effects of Storm Austen, perfect conditions for running rugby in Cape Town led to a mad encounter in which both sides traded blows and line breaks. Stormers led 33-14 at half-time and had their try bonus point secure through efforts by Zachary Porthen, Hasseim Pead, Ntuthuko Mchunu, Seabelo Senatla and Deon Fourie. More efforts followed by Olly Reid and Ahmed, but Scarlets showed fighting spirit and attacking flair. Wales centre Roberts went over three times along with Ioan Jones, Josh Macleod and Macs Page, who was helped from the field after a heavy head injury. Tandy on copping flak and his tough Wales calls Scarlets wing Page tipped for huge Wales future Scarlets, who have never beaten Stormers, scrapped their way to 40-40 in the final quarter and seemed to be in the ascendancy, but failed to make it a hat-trick of wins after successes against Benetton and Newcastle in Llanelli. They now finish the first block of the season with an equally daunting fixture against Bulls in Pretoria on Saturday, 31 October (15:00 GMT). Nigel Davies' side will need to drastically improve their defence and set-piece if they are to stand a chance of upsetting the odds with their expansive approach at Loftus Versfeld. Scarlets were chasing the game from early on after John Dobson's side struck twice when hooker John McKee was yellow-carded for cynically killing the ball in the 11th minute. Tight-head prop Porthen went over from a cunning line-out move followed by a much more dashing second, scrum-half Pead crossing from a sensational Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu offload behind his back. The 14-man Scarlets responded well with Roberts, who missed out on Wales' Nations Championship squad, put over down the right by wing Jones. But that was cancelled out by rampaging loose-head Ntuthuko Mchunu powering over from loose line-out ball. After providing an assist for the first, Jones finished magnificently down the right for Scarlets' second, but once again Stormers hit straight back. Wing Senatla and hooker Fourie scored either side of a second Jones effort being chalked off for a forward pass for a commanding 33-14 lead. A late double by Yaqeen Ahmed sealed victory for the South Africans, with the Llanelli-based side having to be content with a try bonus when they had given themselves a shot at a famous win. While the UK was battered by Storm Boelo and south west Wales was still suffering the effects of Storm Austen, perfect conditions for running rugby in Cape Town led to a mad encounter in which both sides traded blows and line breaks. Stormers led 33-14 at half-time and had their try bonus point secure through efforts by Zachary Porthen, Hasseim Pead, Ntuthuko Mchunu, Seabelo Senatla and Deon Fourie. More efforts followed by Olly Reid and Ahmed, but Scarlets showed fighting spirit and attacking flair.
