Tandy on copping flak and his tough Wales calls Scarlets wing Page tipped for huge Wales future Scarlets, who have never beaten Stormers, scrapped their way to 40-40 in the final quarter and seemed to be in the ascendancy, but failed to make it a hat-trick of wins after successes against Benetton and Newcastle in Llanelli. They now finish the first block of the season with an equally daunting fixture against Bulls in Pretoria on Saturday, 31 October (15:00 GMT). Nigel Davies' side will need to drastically improve their defence and set-piece if they are to stand a chance of upsetting the odds with their expansive approach at Loftus Versfeld. Scarlets were chasing the game from early on after John Dobson's side struck twice when hooker John McKee was yellow-carded for cynically killing the ball in the 11th minute. Tight-head prop Porthen went over from a cunning line-out move followed by a much more dashing second, scrum-half Pead crossing from a sensational Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu offload behind his back. The 14-man Scarlets responded well with Roberts, who missed out on Wales' Nations Championship squad, put over down the right by wing Jones. But that was cancelled out by rampaging loose-head Ntuthuko Mchunu powering over from loose line-out ball. After providing an assist for the first, Jones finished magnificently down the right for Scarlets' second, but once again Stormers hit straight back. Wing Senatla and hooker Fourie scored either side of a second Jones effort being chalked off for a forward pass for a commanding 33-14 lead. Tonga forward Sam Lousi signed for Scarlets in 2019 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] It seemed that Scarlets were already playing for a consolation bonus in a heavy loss, yet it was game on thanks to a pair of quickfire tries after the restart. A searing break by full-back Ioan Nicholas led to in-form wing Page going over and then Roberts intercepted for the four-try bonus. Page was then helped from the field with an oxygen mask after hitting his head heavily on the ground as he attempted to score. Stormers turned to their tight game to regain control, earning penalties to march down the field for prop Reid to score. Scarlets would not go away and it was a seven-point game on the hour after captain Macleod profited from neat handling. They had the momentum and it was level at 40-40 with quarter of an hour to go when Roberts went through midfield for his hat-trick. With Stormers hindered by the absence of a specialist hooker, which led to uncontested scrums, Scarlets scented a famous win. Yet the hosts got their noses back in front in the 73rd minute when Ahmed was worked under the posts and he took away one of Scarlets' bonuses with a late breakaway. How they lined up Stormers: Gelant; Senatla, Simelane, Muller, Zas; Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Pead; Mchunu, Venter, Porthen, Norton, Evans, de Villiers (capt), Roos, Dayimani. Replacements: Vokozela, Reid, Fouche, Smith, Schickerling, Fourie, Reinach, Ahmed. Scarlets: Nicholas; I Jones, J Roberts, Hawkins, Page; Leggatt-Jones, Blacker; Mathias, McKee, Harri O'Connor, Groves, Lousi, Plumtree, Macleod (capt), Anderson. Replacements: G Roberts, S O'Connor, Hawley, Cuckson, Davis, Hughes, Anscombe, Murray-Macgregor. Yellow card: McKee 10. Referee: Robbie Jenkinson (Ireland). Assistant referees: Christopher Allison & Juan de Bod (South Africa). TMO: Eoghan Cross (Ireland).

item.title: Abia govt has abandoned us — Ubani Market traders cry out, seek Otti’s intervention
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Thirteen years after their relocation from the heart of Umuahia to Ubani Ultra-modern Market, thousands of traders are counting their losses, battling dwindling patronage and watching their businesses crumble as they accuse the Abia State Government of abandoning them. From collapsing shops overtaken by weeds to deplorable internal roads, heaps of refuse, poor sanitation and the absence of electricity, water and banking facilities, the once-bustling market has become a symbol of dashed hopes for traders who say their compliance with the government’s relocation order has left them economically stranded. They are now appealing to Governor Alex Otti to urgently intervene before the market, which was conceived as the commercial hub of Umuahia, collapses completely. Their grievances go beyond decaying infrastructure. They include dwindling sales, the exodus of traders, alleged inconsistency in the enforcement of the market relocation policy, the burden of an annual ₦36,000 levy per shop and the absence of a promised alternative access road which traders say could reduce traffic congestion and road accidents. The market, formerly known as Umuahia Daily Market, was relocated from the popular Isigate area of the city in 2013 during the administration of former Governor Theodore Orji. Its former site now houses the Umuahia Central Bus Terminal. When the market was moved to its present location, about seven kilometres from the city centre, between Umuahia and Uzuakoli in Bende Local Government Area, it initially attracted traders and customers in large numbers. The government had justified the relocation as part of efforts to decongest Umuahia and spread development beyond the city centre. It then provided luxury buses to convey traders and customers to the new market at heavily subsidised rates, while shop owners at the old location were allocated land to construct new shops. With more than 10,000 lock-up shops, in addition to thousands of open stalls, the market initially enjoyed considerable patronage. It also had facilities including a fire station, conveniences and security posts. But traders say the initial promise has gradually given way to neglect, with many businesses struggling to survive and some shops abandoned or collapsing. They trace the deterioration partly to what they describe as the failure of successive administrations, particularly that of former Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, to sustain the original relocation policy. According to them, the alleged lax enforcement of the relocation order allowed traders to return to available spaces around Isigate and other parts of the city centre, drawing customers away from Ubani and undermining businesses whose owners had complied with the government’s directive. During a visit to the market by Vanguard, traders recounted painful experiences, describing a deteriorating commercial environment in which some struggle to cover their daily expenses. ‘This market does not look six month
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Thirteen years after their relocation from the heart of Umuahia to Ubani Ultra-modern Market, thousands of traders are counting their losses, battling dwindling patronage and watching their businesses crumble as they accuse the Abia State Government of abandoning them. From collapsing shops overtaken by weeds to deplorable internal roads, heaps of refuse, poor sanitation and the absence of electricity, water and banking facilities, the once-bustling market has become a symbol of dashed hopes for traders who say their compliance with the government’s relocation order has left them economically stranded. They are now appealing to Governor Alex Otti to urgently intervene before the market, which was conceived as the commercial hub of Umuahia, collapses completely. Their grievances go beyond decaying infrastructure. They include dwindling sales, the exodus of traders, alleged inconsistency in the enforcement of the market relocation policy, the burden of an annual ₦36,000 levy per shop and the absence of a promised alternative access road which traders say could reduce traffic congestion and road accidents. The market, formerly known as Umuahia Daily Market, was relocated from the popular Isigate area of the city in 2013 during the administration of former Governor Theodore Orji. Its former site now houses the Umuahia Central Bus Terminal. When the market was moved to its present location, about seven kilometres from the city centre, between Umuahia and Uzuakoli in Bende Local Government Area, it initially attracted traders and customers in large numbers. The government had justified the relocation as part of efforts to decongest Umuahia and spread development beyond the city centre. It then provided luxury buses to convey traders and customers to the new market at heavily subsidised rates, while shop owners at the old location were allocated land to construct new shops. With more than 10,000 lock-up shops, in addition to thousands of open stalls, the market initially enjoyed considerable patronage. It also had facilities including a fire station, conveniences and security posts. But traders say the initial promise has gradually given way to neglect, with many businesses struggling to survive and some shops abandoned or collapsing. They trace the deterioration partly to what they describe as the failure of successive administrations, particularly that of former Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, to sustain the original relocation policy. According to them, the alleged lax enforcement of the relocation order allowed traders to return to available spaces around Isigate and other parts of the city centre, drawing customers away from Ubani and undermining businesses whose owners had complied with the government’s directive. During a visit to the market by Vanguard, traders recounted painful experiences, describing a deteriorating commercial environment in which some struggle to cover their daily expenses. ‘This market does not look six months old’ A provisions dealer, Mr Ugochukwu Okeke, popularly known as Onwa, identified poor internal roads, lack of electricity, declining patronage and the absence of the promised alternative access road via Umueze as major challenges confronting traders. He said the failure to construct the proposed Ubani–Agbo–Umueze Road had continued to expose road users to the dangers of the busy Umuahia–Uzuakoli Road. ” In 2013 when we were asked to relocate to this place, Government promised to build a shorter route to the market passing through Umueze and Agbo to make it easily accessible from the city but up till today we have not seen it. The other day, a trader was returning to the City after the day’s sales and boarded a tricycle. On their way through the busy Uzuakoli road, a trailer had a break failure and rammed into the Keke. The head of the woman was cut off immediately as a result of the impact. That woman wouldn’t have lost her life if the road Ubani-Agbo -Umueze Road were fixed as promised earlier by Government 13 years ago. ” Another challenge we face here is poor sales due to continued decline in the number of people coming to shop here. This is because of the existence of markets around Isigate. Many traders have continued to pull out of the market back to town and government is doing nothing but just watching helplessly. This is affecting the few of us that are here. ” This is 13 years we were forced to come here but this market does not look as if it has lasted for six months because it is going down everyday.” Beyond the physical deterioration, Okeke said the absence of banks in and around the market had created security risks for traders who handle cash from daily sales. He recalled an incident in which a neighbouring trader allegedly lost a carton containing money after hiding it among refuse to prevent thieves from stealing the proceeds of his business. ” My neighbour sometime ago lost his carton of money here. He was putting the proceeds of the day’s sales inside the cartoon and kept it in the midst of refuse to avoid being stolen because there is no Bank in the market. Afterwards he collected a carton of refuse thinking it was the one containing money. On getting home he discovered he had forgotten his money outside and tili today he has not found it back.” The trader also faulted the collection of an annual consolidated levy of ₦36,000 per shop, saying the financial burden had become difficult to bear amid poor sales.He appealed to the government to make the levy payable per trader rather than per shop, as he said was currently the practice. ” Last year they came and said we will be paying N36,000 per annum promising to use the revenue to solve our problems. We paid. The worst thing is that they are collecting this revenue based on the number of shops a trader has in the market. Although we pay, we don’t yet see anything they are doing with it. ” I’m not sure the Governor is aware of this. That’s why I’m appealing to him to look into what is happening at Ubani Ultra-modern Market. We are suffering here. We are just merely surviving by God’s grace. There is no future for this market as long as the same Government continues to allow some traders return to Isigate. We heard that revenue collectors collect revenues from the traders there twice a day. That’s why they are not serious about forcing them out of that place. We are the ones suffering it here”. ‘Our business capital is depreciating’ A patent medicine dealer, Mr Michael Ubani, said the market’s fortunes would continue to decline unless the government enforced its relocation policy and addressed the infrastructure deficit. He said traders who obeyed the relocation directive had been left to bear the consequences while competing markets continued to operate within the city centre. ” We are hopelessly struggling to survive here. This is a stranded place for us because of its distance from the City metropolis. Government is not looking our way. Every effort to get Government’s attention to this market has been fruitless. You can see that traders are pulling from the market on daily basis due to lack of patronage. ” Amenities here are zero – no internal roads, no electricity. The Umueze – Agbo -Ubani road which would have provided a shorter route to the market is a total mess. We are regretting complying with Government’s order to relocate from town to this place 13 years ago. Our business capital is depreciating. You hardly cover your daily expenses here and that is why many traders are existing the market back to town.” Ubani recalled that traders had protested at Government House last year in an attempt to draw the government’s attention to their plight. According to him, although the then Commissioner for Trade and Investment promised to convey their complaints to the governor, the promised intervention had yet to materialise. item.title: Fulham climb out of drop zone after Oscar Bobb’s late show sinks Coventry
item.description: Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a win against Coventry that lifted Álvaro Arbeloa’s side clear of the relegation zone. Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to score in the 80th minute, twisting his way into the area and bending a shot into the far corner. It was his second goal for the club since his £27m move from Manchester City in January. Continue reading...

item.title: Clinical Arsenal earn precious win against Everton thanks to Konsa and Gabriel
item.description: The wait goes on for David Moyes. The Scot must have been hoping that, on his 14th visit to this stadium as Everton’s manager, his luck would finally change. Yet from the moment Ezri Konsa slammed home his first goal for Arsenal as the Premier League champions rediscovered their knack of scoring from set pieces, the writing was on the wall for Moyes against his former captain, Mikel Arteta. While it took until midway through the second half for Gabriel Magalhães to make sure of the victory, Arsenal never looked likely to let slip the chance of moving level on points at the top with Manchester City after their defeat by Aston Villa earlier in the day. This was hardly a vintage performance from Arteta’s clinical side but it didn’t need to be against opponents who offered precious little in attack, even if they defended for their lives at times. Having gone six matches without defeat to start the season, a second in succession will only add to Moyes’s concerns after confirmation that the club’s American owners want out. Continue reading...

item.title: 5 Hardest Platformers Ever Made, Ranked by Difficulty
item.description: Platform games have an undeniable innocence. Since the days of Super Mario Bros. , they've embodied the escapist joy that people associate with the medium. It's hard not to be charmed by the colorful aesthetics, creative styles, and beautifully simple gameplay. Sure, plenty of other genres have emerged over the years, but none have captured the easygoing appeal of running and jumping over obstacles. That pure sense of fun makes platformers the ultimate gaming comfort food . On the other hand, not every bite is so sweet.

item.title: 2027: Opposition has upgraded campaign from Facebook, Twitter to AI – Gov. Sani
item.description: .Tells ‘northern candidate’: Show us your track record By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State has declared that the opposition has upgraded its campaign from Facebook and Twitter to Artificial Intelligence AI, warning supporters of his ruling All Progressives Congress APC to be wary of the development. He spoke on Saturday in Kaduna at the flag-off of the APC presidential campaign. “The opposition have now upgraded their campaign from Facebook and Twitter to AI. So, I want to call the attention of our supporters to prepare, be watchful and be vigilant,” the governor said. In apparent reference to former vice w Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, Sani challenged the “northern candidate” to show his track record. “When someone came to us and said we should vote for him simply because he is a Northerner, we asked him, ‘Can you show us your track record?’ Until this moment, the so-called Northern candidate has not shown us his track record, Mr President. No track record, and we keep asking,” he said. He spoke on Saturday in Kaduna at the flag-off of the APC presidential campaign. “The opposition have now upgraded their campaign from Facebook and Twitter to AI. So, I want to call the attention of our supporters to prepare, be watchful and be vigilant,” the governor said. In apparent reference to former vice w Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, Sani challenged the “northern candidate” to show his track record. “When someone came to us and said we should vote for him simply because he is a Northerner, we asked him, ‘Can you show us your track record?’ Until this moment, the so-called Northern candidate has not shown us his track record, Mr President. No track record, and we keep asking,” he said. He said he had told Vice President Kashmir Shettima at the airport that history would remember him. “I pointed out to him that, as Vice President under you, more than 1,000 kilometres of roads have already been constructed in the northern part of Nigeria,” Sani said. Turning to the “northern candidate” again, he asked: “Can you show us 200 kilometres of road that you were able to help the people of the North East with while you were Vice President? Till this moment, we have not seen one.” The governor said the people of Kaduna and the North were ready to repay the president at the polls. “That is why today we are affirming our resolve as a people to massively come out in January 2027 to vote for continuity. We are voting for a promise keeper to continue with the good work he is already doing in Kaduna State and in general,” he said. Speaking on behalf of the governors present, particularly those from the North, he added: “I want to thank you, Mr President, and assure you that the people of Northern Nigeria will repay you with their votes. You have seen, Mr President, the people coming from the airport to the stadium. Some people will come out on January 16 to vote for you.” Sani recalled that Tinubu visited Birnin Gwari Local Government Area as a candidate on December 22, 2022, when it was “the epicentre of insecurity in the whole of the North-West”, and rejected advice not to go. The journey from Kaduna took four hours, with 27 armoured vehicles in the convoy. “Mr President, today I can assure you that the two promises you made have been fulfilled,” he said. He said the Kaduna-Birnin Gwari road, “a 123km road that had been abandoned for over 40 years”, is being reconstructed, with N117bn released to the contractor. “Today, you can travel to Birnin Gwari with your eyes closed without a single police escort, Mr President. That is progress, Mr President,” he said. On the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano Expressway, the governor said the president had assured him he would pay the N740bn for its reconstruction. “As we are speaking, Mr President, 95 per cent of the work has been completed,” he said. He added that more than 90 per cent of Kaduna residents who came to the venue through the Abuja route “have not experienced a single problem of kidnapping”. Sani also thanked the president for choosing Kaduna as the pilot state for the metropolitan red line project. He said $865m had been approved, and that the contractor, Mota-Engil, told him last week it had mobilised $300m for the corridor of about 50km. On agriculture, he said: “No leader in the history of Nigeria has supported agricultural transformation as substantially as you have done, Mr President, and that is a record.” The Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council PCC, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, said the campaign would be built on the government’s record. “We Nigerians, at the head of this campaign, are going to campaign with our records. Our records are there. The infrastructure is there. What you did in health, education and human capital development is there,” he said. Yari said the party had been engaging traditional rulers, ulama and imams on the importance of the president’s return in 2027. “Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent for you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, by God’s grace. And the promise we have made, you are going to see it on January 16, 2027,” Yari said. The post 2027: Opposition has upgraded campaign from Facebook, Twitter to AI – Gov. item.title: Shun partisan politics, Aiyedatiwa tells Ondo corps members
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has charged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) deployed to the state to avoid partisan politics in their host communities. Aiyedatiwa gave the charge at the closing ceremony and terminal parade of the 2026 Batch C Stream I orientation course held at Ikare-Akoko. Represented by the State Coordinator of the scheme, Mrs Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, the governor urged the corps members to be conscious of their responsibilities. “Remain mindful of the responsibilities that come with your position as corps members. Your actions will reflect not only on you but also on your families, your institutions and the NYSC,” he said. He appealed to employers and heads of establishments to receive corps members posted to them with cooperation and understanding. “Provide them with a conducive working environment, appropriate guidance and opportunities to contribute their knowledge and skills. Your mentorship can help them grow professionally and gain valuable experience that will serve them well beyond their service year,” Aiyedatiwa said. He also called on local government authorities, traditional rulers and community leaders to support corps members in their areas to aid their integration and effective execution of Community Development Service projects. “Your cooperation is essential to their successful integration into host communities and to the effective implementation of Community Development Service projects. By working together, we can ensure that the presence of corps members translates into tangible benefits for the people of Ondo State,” he added. The governor further urged the corps members to accept their postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for their host communities. “Approach your responsibilities with a strong sense of duty. Accept your postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for the people among whom you will live and work. Be willing to learn from your host communities, respect their customs and cultural values and conduct yourselves in ways that will earn their trust and confidence. “Your service year should be about more than fulfilling an obligation. It should be an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to society,” he said. Aiyedatiwa assured that his administration will continue to collaborate with security agencies and other stakeholders to ensure a safe environment for corps members throughout the service year. He cautioned them against compromising their personal security, advising them to remain vigilant, avoid late-night movements and unsafe gatherings, and shun unsolicited rides from strangers. “Be cautious when visiting unfamiliar or isolated places and promptly report suspicious activities or security concerns to the appropriate authorities. “Shun drug abuse, cybercrime, fraud and other unlawful activities that could jeopardise your future and bring disrepute to the scheme,” the governor added.

item.title: Jackson Fires Villa To Victory, Ends Man City’s Perfect Start
item.description: Manchester City’s perfect Premier League start came to a crashing halt in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa as Nicolas Jackson’s double extended an upturn in form for Unai Emery’s new-look side. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. After Jackson blasted home the opener after just six minutes, Villa relied on a brilliant goalkeeping display from Zion Suzuki to keep City at bay. Erling Haaland breifly levelled early in the second half only for Villa to respond on the hour mark when Jackson drilled home Ibrahim Mbaye’s cross. “A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park,” said Emery. “We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic.” Manchester City’s Norwegian striker #09 Erling Haaland headers at goal but the shot is saved during the English Premier League football match between Aston Villa and Manchester City at Villa Park in Birmingham, central England on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) Four years on from Emery’s arrival, which has transformed the club from a sleeping giant into the Champions League, the Spaniard is working more magic despite seeing the spine of his squad in recent seasons decimated. “He’s just a tactical genius,” Villa full-back Maty Cash said of his manager. “He’s always got a new plan for something. He’s always coming up with new ideas.” Six of the side that started Villa’s victory in last season’s Europa League final left during the transfer window. But the recruitment of Jackson, Suzuki, Mbaye and Johan Manzambi is already paying dividends after a slow start to the campaign. Until now City have managed to shrug off the cloud hanging over the club’s Premier League future to keep winning on the field. The 10-time English champions are appealing a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 that could lead to swingeing sanctions, including relegation. There was little sign of that distraction affecting Maresca’s men, but they were made to pay for two sloppy defensive errors. Manchester City’s Norwegian striker #09 Erling Haaland headers the ball to scores the equalising goal during the English Premier League football match between Aston Villa and Manchester City at Villa Park in Birmingham, central England on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) “I think we deserved more from the game for the amount of chances that we created and for the chances we conceded,” said Maresca. “We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box.” A heavy touch by Marc Guehi presented Jackson with possession for the opening goal as he cut inside Elliott Anderson and blasted high past Gianluigi Donnarumma. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) “I think we deserved more from the game for the amount of chances that we created and for the chances we conceded,” said Maresca. “We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box.” A heavy touch by Marc Guehi presented Jackson with possession for the opening goal as he cut inside Elliott Anderson and blasted high past Gianluigi Donnarumma. City largely dominated the remainder of the first half, but could not find a way past Suzuki. Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov were all denied before Ndiaye struck the post. City’s pressure finally told on 52 minutes when Haaland powered in a header from Ndiaye’s cross for his 13th goal in 10 appearances this season. Josko Gvardiol nearly completed the comeback when Suzuki turned his blistering drive into the crossbar moments later. Instead, it was Villa to got the decisive third goal. item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
item.description: null On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film. When they saw the images for the first time, the scientists were literally jumping up and down with joy. This photo is the first view of Earth from space taken by a camera on a U.S. Army V-2 rocket launched from White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico on Oct. 24, 1946. (Image credit: U.S. Army) How it mattered The ability to photograph Earth from space drove both an expanded interest to continue pushing into space and led to unexpected societal changes with regards to how humanity considered its home planet. For military and intelligence agencies, the potential now existed for reconnaissance at a far larger scale than what was possible with high-altitude aircraft. That capability expanded to agriculture and meteorological purposes, eventually making Earth observation one of the most common reasons satellites and space stations are deployed into orbit today. Earth photography from space also gave birth to the environmental movement, as people began to see the planet differently. The fragility of this orb became more apparent, as now Earth appeared a "blue marble" set against an endless black void. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.description: The global design world just got a major dose of Lagos energy! In a historic moment for the African creative scene, the world-renowned Salone del Mobile . Milano officially touched down in Nigeria for the very first time during Design Week Lagos 2026. Held at the iconic National Theatre, the high-profile gathering brought together international design heavyweights, top Nigerian architects, interior designers, business leaders, and cultural icons for an unforgettable exchange of ideas and inspiration. Leading the Italian delegation were Marco Sabetta , General Manager, Salone del Mobile and the legendary Marva Griffin Wilshire, Founder & Curator, SaloneSatellite. The strategic visit highlights Nigeria’s booming demand for luxury design and luxury living, with demand for Italian craftsmanship reaching record highs across the continent. Honors & Cultural Magic A major highlight of the week was the inaugural IDEA Honours, where Marva Griffin Wilshire received the Architectural Legacy Honour—complete with a breathtaking custom award plaque crafted by iconic Nigerian master Demas Nwoko , MFR. Also celebrated were visionary architect Lesley Lokko and celebrated artist Yinka Shonibare CBE. “Being here in Lagos today allowed us to discover remarkable new African talent and build the conditions that will help young designers forge their paths globally, ” shared an inspired Marva Griffin Wilshire. Making a New Africa From guided exhibition tours to rich panel sessions focused on this year’s theme, Making a New Africa: From Material to Market, the atmosphere was charged with ambition and creativity. Design Week Lagos founder Titi Ogufer e emphasized that Africa’s rich materials, heritage, and creative talent are ready to drive global industrial growth. With Design Week Lagos running through October 25th, the city has firmly cemented its status as Africa’s ultimate capital for design, innovation, and style. Next stop? Milan for the 65th edition of Salone del Mobile in April 2027! item.title: One of 2026’s Best-Rated Games Is Basically Mass Effect With Spies
item.description: This week's news that EA was shutting down Mass Effect developer BioWare and canceling the next game in the series was a blow to the industry. It was made all the worse when a leaked trailer for the game, known as Mass Effect: Universe , showed exactly what we would all be missing: Mass Effect meets James Bond . That sure is an enticing pitch, and while BioWare will never be able to deliver on what the trailer teased, that also describes one of this year's best games.

item.title: LG’s brilliant C6 OLED TV is already $400 off ahead of Black Friday
item.description: LG’s C6 OLED TV is on sale in multiple sizes starting at $999.99 ($300 off). | Image: LG Black Friday is still over a month away, but if you’re hoping to upgrade your TV, you don’t need to wait until November. LG has already kicked off its early Black Friday sale , letting you save on the LG C6 and various soundbars through November 1st. Right now, for instance, you can snag a 55-inch C6 for an all-time low of $999.99 ($400 off) , with Amazon and Best Buy matching said price. Other sizes are also discounted, including the 65-inch model, which is on sale for $1,399.99 ($300 off) from Amazon , Best Buy , and LG . If you purchase direct, you’ll also get a free Xbox Wireless Controller and a complimentary wall mount. LG C6 OLED TV Where to Buy: $1399.99 $999.99 at Amazon (55-inch) $1699.99 $1399.99 at Amazon (65-inch) $2499.99 $1999.99 at Amazon (77-inch) LG’s C6 OLED TV offers a few small but welcome upgrades over last year’s C5, including a faster Alpha 11 AI Gen3 processor designed to improve picture and sound quality, along with a brighter display. It also boasts a higher refresh rate of up to 165Hz for smoother gaming, up from 144Hz, while retaining four HDMI 2.1 ports and support for AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync, the latter of which helps reduce unwanted screen tearing while gaming. Unsurprisingly, the C6 delivers the hallmarks of OLED technology, including inky blacks, vibrant color, and impressive contrast. Support for Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, meanwhile, helps make movies and shows appear more lifelike and immersive, while built-in access to Netflix, HBO Max, and the like lets you stream your favorite content without a dedicated streaming device. Google Cast and Apple AirPlay 2 also make it easy to share content from your phone, while Matter support lets you pair it with various smart home devices. Solid specs aside, we’d be remiss not to mention that researchers recently raised concerns about how LG’s smart TVs collect and log user data. LG has since responded to some of the accusations , saying its TVs don’t continuously record conversations, and that features like voice recognition and interest-based advertising are optional and disabled by default. While LG hasn’t addressed all concerns, similar data-collection practices aren’t necessarily unique to LG TVs, and they don’t detract from the C6’s impressive feature set.

item.title: Tinubu, Shettima flag off APC 2027 campaign in Kaduna
item.description: President Bola Tinubu arrived in Kaduna State on Saturday ahead of the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress’ 2027 presidential campaign, with Vice President Kashim Shettima and his wife, Nana, also arriving for the event. APC National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, the Director-General of the presidential campaign, Abdul’aziz Yari, and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani were at the airport to welcome the President. Shettima’s arrival was announced in a statement by his spokesman, Stanley Nkwocha. Mr Nkwocha said APC governors, party leaders, elected officials, political stakeholders and supporters were gathering at the Kaduna Township Stadium for the commencement of the party’s nationwide presidential campaign. He described the event as a significant moment for Kaduna, noting that the city would serve as the launching point for the APC’s campaign ahead of the 2027 presidential election. According to the statement, the campaign would provide the ruling party with an opportunity to present its “Renewed Hope 2.0” agenda and highlight the achievements of the Tinubu administration. “The stage is set. Kaduna is ready. The 2027 campaign begins!” the statement read in part. It added, “Asiwaju is here. Northwest for the takeaway!” Ahead of the President’s arrival, security operatives on Saturday barricaded strategic locations across Kaduna metropolis as authorities stepped up security preparations for the campaign event. Personnel from the Nigerian Army, Department of State Services, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Nigeria Immigration Service and the Kaduna State Vigilance Service were deployed to different parts of the city. The security personnel were stationed at major roundabouts and along roads leading to the venue of the campaign flag-off. Muhammadu Buhari Way, formerly known as WAFF Road, was blocked by security operatives ahead of the expected movement of the President and his entourage through the route. The Ahmadu Bello Stadium roundabout was also manned by heavily armed soldiers, police officers and plain-clothes security personnel. The security restrictions affected traffic in several parts of Kaduna, triggering a gridlock that extended from Junction Road to Ahmadu Bello Way. The post Tinubu, Shettima flag off APC 2027 campaign in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: French Montana, Jorja Smith to perform at Ballon d’Or 2026
item.description: Ballon d’Or organisers revealed on Saturday that star US rapper French Montana and English singer Jorja Smith would perform at this year’s ceremony, part of efforts to draw more viewers to the awards event. Last year saw Canadian singer Charlotte Cardin do her best to lift the somewhat stiff atmosphere at the prize giving in Paris as she performed her hit “Feel Good” in front of a motionless crowd of suited footballers and VIPs at a theatre. The most prestigious individual award in football will be handed out in London next Monday, with Kylian Mbappe, Spanish pair Lamine Yamal and Ferran Torres, PSG duo Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Harry Kane all seen as frontrunners. It is the first time the Ballon d’Or ceremony, now in its 70th edition, will be hosted in Britain. French Montana has over 30 million monthly listeners on Spotify, mixing Moroccan influences, trap, afrobeat and New York hip hop culture. He has collaborated on hits with Drake, Cardi B and Swae Lee, with whom he made the 2017 track “Unforgettable”, which has racked up 1.9 billion views on YouTube. English singer-songwriter Jorja Smith mixes RnB, soul and jazz influences, drawing on her Jamaican heritage and her classical music training. Her career took off 10 years ago with “Blue Lights”, followed by other tracks ranging from intimate to more danceable. In addition to their “exclusive performances” during the evening, “other surprises are planned”, the Groupe L’Equipe, which organises the ceremony, said in a statement sent to AFP. The group owns the magazine France Football, which has been awarding the Ballon d’Or since 1956. It is based on voting by a jury of journalists from the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings. In 2025, the top male player prize was awarded to France’s Ousmane Dembele and the women’s to Spain’s Aitana Bonmati. The ceremony will be broadcast on sports streaming website DAZN, and the L’Equipe TV channel in France. It will be hosted by former France and Arsenal striker Thierry Henry, and sports journalist Kate Scott. In 2022, tenor Andrea Bocelli was chosen to open the ceremony. After last year’s event, Quebec-born Cardin revealed that she had felt uneasy, explaining that she had been through a “moment of great solitude” when she performed alone with limited lighting and stage effects. fan-adp/gil The post French Montana, Jorja Smith to perform at Ballon d’Or 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NFL's Paris Premier: Saints RB Alvin Kamara on global reach, sport as catalyst for youth opportunity
item.description: François Picard and Selina Sykes are pleased to welcome New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara. As the National Football League expands its international ambitions to Paris, FRANCE, Kamara offers a unique perspective that reaches well beyond the spectacle of American football's arrival in the French capital. Just days before the Saints' anticipated encounter with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Kamara describes the occasion as "an opportunity unlike any other," while reflecting on his remarkable career, his interest in representing his country in flag football at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, and his ambitions to develop sporting opportunities in Liberia, his parents' country of birth.

item.title: NDC fixes October 26 for 3rd NEC meeting, campaign council unveiling
item.description: …Says 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms By Henry Umoru The national leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has fixed Monday, October 26, for its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting, where it will unveil its National Campaign Council and present its candidates with Certificates of Return. The party has attributed its limited financial resources partly to the economic hardship in the country, just as it claimed that about 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms. According to the NDC, it had to issue the forms to the affected candidates free of charge, contrary to what he described as public speculation about its finances. In a statement signed on Saturday by NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, he disclosed that the meeting would also feature the presentation of the party’s statement of account by its National Treasurer. According to him, it is part of the party’s commitment to transparency and accountability in the management of its finances, just as it challenged other political parties, particularly the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to adopt similar measures in disclosing their financial records, adding, “For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual.” The statement read, “The leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) wishes to announce that its 3rd National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting will hold on Monday, 26th October, 2026, at JD event centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, opposite A-class park, Maitama, Abuja. Time is 10 am prompt. “A major highlight of the meeting will be the release and presentation of the party’s Statement of Account by the National Treasurer. This is in deference to our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability. In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in the management of their finances. “For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual. “Our finances would have been more robust. However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms. The party had to issue forms to such candidates free of charge. “The party will also use the opportunity of the NEC meeting to unveil its National Campaign Council (NCC). “As a party of innovation, our NCC is all-encompassing. It covers the Presidential, National Assembly, Governorship, and State Houses of Assembly Campaign Councils. “Our various candidates will be presented with Certificates of Return for their respective offices. “The NDC is turbo-charged and ready to give Nigerians the altruistic leadership the nation deserves. A New Nigeria is Possible. We can do it!” The post NDC fixes Oct

According to him, it is part of the party’s commitment to transparency and accountability in the management of its finances, just as it challenged other political parties, particularly the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to adopt similar measures in disclosing their financial records, adding, “For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual.” The statement read, “The leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) wishes to announce that its 3rd National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting will hold on Monday, 26th October, 2026, at JD event centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, opposite A-class park, Maitama, Abuja. Time is 10 am prompt. “A major highlight of the meeting will be the release and presentation of the party’s Statement of Account by the National Treasurer. This is in deference to our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability. In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in the management of their finances. “For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual. “Our finances would have been more robust. However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms. The party had to issue forms to such candidates free of charge. “The party will also use the opportunity of the NEC meeting to unveil its National Campaign Council (NCC). “As a party of innovation, our NCC is all-encompassing. It covers the Presidential, National Assembly, Governorship, and State Houses of Assembly Campaign Councils. “Our various candidates will be presented with Certificates of Return for their respective offices. “The NDC is turbo-charged and ready to give Nigerians the altruistic leadership the nation deserves. A New Nigeria is Possible. We can do it!” The post NDC fixes October 26 for 3rd NEC meeting, campaign council unveiling appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Man City beaten by Aston Villa to end perfect Premier League start
item.description: Manchester City’s perfect Premier League start came to a crashing halt in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa as Nicolas Jackson’s double extended an upturn in form for Unai Emery’s new-look side. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. After Jackson blasted home the opener after just six minutes, Villa relied on a brilliant goalkeeping display from Zion Suzuki to keep City at bay. Erling Haaland breifly levelled early in the second half only for Villa to respond on the hour mark when Jackson drilled home Ibrahim Mbaye’s cross. Four years on from Emery’s arrival, which has transformed the club from a sleeping giant into the Champions League, the Spaniard is working more magic despite seeing the spine of his squad in recent seasons decimated. Six of the side that started Villa’s victory in last season’s Europa League left during the transfer window. But the recruitment of the likes of Jackson, Suzuki, Mbaye and Johan Manzambi is already paying dividends after a slow start to the campaign. Until now City have managed to shrug off the cloud hanging over the club’s Premier League future to keep winning on the field. The 10-time English champions are appealing a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 that could lead to swingeing sanctions, including relegation. There was little sign of that distraction affecting Enzo Maresca’s men, but they were made to pay for two sloppy defensive errors. A heavy touch by Marc Guehi presented Jackson with possession for the opening goal as he cut inside Elliott Anderson and blasted high past Gianluigi Donnarumma. City largely dominated the remainder of the first half, but could not find a way past Suzuki. Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov were all denied before Ndiaye struck the post. City’s pressure finally told on 52 minutes when Haaland powered in a header from Ndiaye’s cross for his 13th goal in 10 appearances this season. Josko Gvardiol nearly completed the comeback when Suzuki turned his blistering drive into the crossbar moments later. Instead, it was Villa to got the decisive third goal. Mbaye was played in behind the City defence and from his cross, Jackson’s low effort should have been saved by Donnarumma. The visitors pressed in vain for another equaliser to allow Arsenal the chance to move level on points at the top of the table when they host Everton later on Saturday. A sixth win in seven games in all competitions for Villa lifts them up to sixth. The post Man City beaten by Aston Villa to end perfect Premier League start appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: The Lenovo Yoga 9n is a pricey workstation laptop, but being a 2-in-1 also makes it fun. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge It looks like the long-rumored touchscreen MacBook might actually get announced next week , and after using the Lenovo Yoga 9n for our testing of Nvidia's RTX Spark platform, it got me thinking: this is a lot of what I want from a touchscreen MacBook. item.title: A Royal Love Story! Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi’s Edo Traditional Wedding Looks
item.description: Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi holding hands during their Edo traditional wedding, styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon. What a beautiful day for love! Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi are celebrating their traditional wedding today, and we’re starting the day with their beautiful first look. The Afrobeats star and his bride-to-be have chosen to honour Davita’s Edo heritage with coordinated traditional wedding attire, from her richly embellished burgundy gown to his regal ivory outfit. And there’s so much to love about the details. For their first appearance, Zlatan, whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , and Davita chose to honour her Edo heritage. And what better way to celebrate love than by showing up in outfits that tell a beautiful story about where you come from? Zlatan Ibile kissing Davita Omoniyi’s hand in their custom Edo cultural attire, styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon. Davita looked every inch the Edo bride in a custom burgundy gown by Dova Bridals. The corseted mermaid design featured a curved sweetheart neckline, sheer long sleeves and a sweeping side train. Red crystal beads formed beautiful lattice patterns across the gown, while her traditional Okuku braided crown and layers of coral necklaces completed the look. She also carried a black horsehair fly whisk, with a sheer crimson veil draped over her crown. Davita Omoniyi as an Edo bride seated on a carved throne in a custom Dova Bridals gown. And Zlatan? The groom was every bit as regal beside his bride. He wore a custom cream robe by Deji & Kola, topped with a textured ivory coat featuring hand-stitched red beadwork along the shoulders and hem. The red details tied his outfit beautifully to Davita’s, while layers of coral beads, an ivory ceremonial cap and a carved wooden staff completed his traditional look. Zlatan Ibile wearing a custom Deji & Kola cream robe and layered coral beads for his traditional wedding. Styled by Goodnews Emmanuel Icon, the couple posed against a warm ombré backdrop, with Zlatan seated on a carved gold throne beneath a tasseled umbrella. Between the coordinated outfits, the traditional accessories and the beautiful celebration of Davita’s Edo roots, their first wedding look is one we’ll be admiring for a while. Zlatan Ibile seated on a ceremonial throne beside Davita Omoniyi for their traditional wedding feature. Caption: Davita Omoniyi wearing a red sheer veil over her traditional Okuku crown for her wedding look. Davita Omoniyi in a burgundy Dova Bridals gown walking with Zlatan Ibile in a Deji & Kola outfit. *** Photo Credit: Zlatan Ibile/Instagram The post A Royal Love Story! Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi’s Edo Traditional Wedding Looks appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: 2027: Atiku is North’s enemy, says Akume
item.description: ….Says, power rotation agreed in Kaduna to keep Nigeria one By Omeiza Ajayi, Kaduna As the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) flagged off its presidential campaign on Saturday in Kaduna, Secretary to the Government of the Federation SGF, Senator George Akume, declared that any northerner seeking to contest the 2027 presidential election is an enemy of the region. Former vice president Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress ADC is the only prominent northern politician seeking to wrestle power from incumbent President Bola Tinubu in the next year’s presidential contest. This was as he reminded Northerners that the agreement on power rotation between the North and the South was reached in Kaduna State to keep the country together. His spokesman, Yomi Odunuga, in a statement on Saturday, said the SGF spoke at a pre-campaign meeting with a large crowd of Benue State indigenes residing in Kaduna. “Remember that it was in this same Kaduna State that we agreed on power rotation between the North and the South. You cannot doubt the credentials of those that reached this agreement at that time, and it was done to keep this country together. We agreed on power shift, and that is what has kept this country going. That is what has retained our territorial integrity,” Akume said. On that basis, he declared that any Northerner seeking to contest the 2027 presidential election is an enemy of the North, insisting that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu remains the right candidate to lead Nigeria beyond 2027. “Anybody who is from the North and running for the presidency is an enemy of the North. Don’t allow that pretender to deceive you. It is not yet our turn. The North’s turn is in 2031. Prepare to vote for Tinubu. Do not allow anyone to destroy the country because of a vaunting personal ambition,” he said. The SGF urged the North to back Tinubu’s re-election bid and wait until 2031 before seeking to return to the presidency. He warned that individual political ambitions should not be allowed to undermine the region’s collective interests. Akume, a former Governor of Benue State, urged Northerners to remain united and resist political manoeuvres capable of weakening the region’s influence. He cautioned against attempts to divide them along political, religious and personal lines, and recalled past political disagreements among Nigerian leaders, warning against repeating mistakes that could weaken the North in national politics. He said the North stands to benefit more from supporting Tinubu’s second-term ambition than from allowing individual political interests to create divisions ahead of the next general elections. Defending the president’s record, the SGF said Tinubu has been fair to all in appointments and does not favour one religion over another. “Let us remember that the President has been fair to all in terms of appointments and others. item.content:encoded: ….Says, power rotation agreed in Kaduna to keep Nigeria one By Omeiza Ajayi, Kaduna As the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) flagged off its presidential campaign on Saturday in Kaduna, Secretary to the Government of the Federation SGF, Senator George Akume, declared that any northerner seeking to contest the 2027 presidential election is an enemy of the region. Former vice president Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress ADC is the only prominent northern politician seeking to wrestle power from incumbent President Bola Tinubu in the next year’s presidential contest. This was as he reminded Northerners that the agreement on power rotation between the North and the South was reached in Kaduna State to keep the country together. His spokesman, Yomi Odunuga, in a statement on Saturday, said the SGF spoke at a pre-campaign meeting with a large crowd of Benue State indigenes residing in Kaduna. “Remember that it was in this same Kaduna State that we agreed on power rotation between the North and the South. You cannot doubt the credentials of those that reached this agreement at that time, and it was done to keep this country together. We agreed on power shift, and that is what has kept this country going. That is what has retained our territorial integrity,” Akume said. On that basis, he declared that any Northerner seeking to contest the 2027 presidential election is an enemy of the North, insisting that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu remains the right candidate to lead Nigeria beyond 2027. “Anybody who is from the North and running for the presidency is an enemy of the North. Don’t allow that pretender to deceive you. It is not yet our turn. The North’s turn is in 2031. Prepare to vote for Tinubu. Do not allow anyone to destroy the country because of a vaunting personal ambition,” he said. The SGF urged the North to back Tinubu’s re-election bid and wait until 2031 before seeking to return to the presidency. He warned that individual political ambitions should not be allowed to undermine the region’s collective interests. Akume, a former Governor of Benue State, urged Northerners to remain united and resist political manoeuvres capable of weakening the region’s influence. He cautioned against attempts to divide them along political, religious and personal lines, and recalled past political disagreements among Nigerian leaders, warning against repeating mistakes that could weaken the North in national politics. He said the North stands to benefit more from supporting Tinubu’s second-term ambition than from allowing individual political interests to create divisions ahead of the next general elections. Defending the president’s record, the SGF said Tinubu has been fair to all in appointments and does not favour one religion over another. “Let us remember that the President has been fair to all in terms of appointments and others. He doesn’t favour one religion over the other. Just look at the figures. So be careful about what people tell you,” he said. Akume also told his audience that the president has shown his love for Benue State through significant projects. “Let nobody deceive you; Asiwaju loves Benue, and he has displayed that in the number of significant projects the Federal Government is carrying out simultaneously in the state. These projects are diverse in healthcare, roads, education and others. This is being replicated throughout the federation. For example, in the area of education, over 65 per cent of NELFUND has been accessed, and most of them are from the North,” he said. Apparently taking a swipe at Atiku, he said, “Forget that other one making noise that he was going to remove fuel subsidy. He is always flip-flopping. He says something today and changes gear the next minute.” The SGF praised Governor Uba Sani and called for his return to office. “Kaduna State is a historic city that gave us meaning and purpose. So, this is your home too, as Benue State citizens living here. The present governor, Senator Uba Sani, believes in that vision of Saudauna. He is a great man. I want to appeal to you that there is none like Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2027. “I was the governor of Benue State, and the Fulanis were there. It is about leadership. If Asiwaju was not a good leader, I would not tell you otherwise. I will still come to Kaduna to speak with you. Your governor is a good man, and he has done well for this state. Let us return him to power too,” he said. The SGF also stressed the need for national unity, peaceful coexistence and cooperation among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups and encouraged the preservation of cultural identity and traditions as a means of promoting understanding among communities. “I believe you are here because you believe in me and because you want to see your son, and that is me in flesh and blood,” he told the gathering. Those who accompanied Akume included a former governor of Jigawa State, Alhaji Saminu Turaki; Dame Pauline Tallen; Senator Abu Ibrahim; the Minister of Water Resources, Prof. Joseph Utsev; and the Minister of Steel Development, Prince Shuaibu Abubakar Audu. item.title: Israeli forces displace 1,200 Palestinians in Hebron after deadly attack on soldiers
item.description: The Palestinian Authority has called for international pressure on Israel after a Palestinian official said around 1,200 Palestinians in Hebron in the West Bank were forced to leave their homes following an attack on Friday which killed two Israeli soldiers. item.title: Troops neutralise 15 terrorists in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), has recorded another operational success with the neutralisation of 15 terrorists in a precision air strike north-west of Pulka in Gwoza LGA of Borno State. According to the Media Information Officer Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni, in a press statement on Saturday, said, “The operation was conducted at about 11:50 p.m. on 23 October 2026, following credible intelligence and confirmed sightings of terrorist movements in the general area of Pulka. “The precision strike was subsequently followed by ground operations to exploit the area and consolidate the operational gains. “The successful engagement highlights the effectiveness of intelligence-driven targeting and coordinated military action in disrupting terrorist movements and degrading their operational capabilities. “It also reflects the unwavering commitment of Operation HADIN KAI to denying terrorist groups freedom of action and preventing them from threatening communities within the theatre. “The operation forms part of the sustained offensive posture of troops, supported by effective intelligence gathering and coordinated employment of available military capabilities. Through these efforts, the Theatre Command continues to maintain pressure on terrorist elements, disrupt their activities and strengthen the security environment across the Northeast. “Operation HADIN KAI remains resolute in its mission to defeat terrorism and insurgency, protect law-abiding citizens and create the conditions necessary for the restoration of normalcy and socio-economic activities in affected communities. “The Theatre Command reassures the public that troops will sustain the momentum of ongoing operations with vigilance, determination and professionalism. “The Theatre Command also calls on members of the public to sustain their cooperation with security agencies by providing timely and credible information on suspicious movements and activities. The continued partnership between the military and the civilian population remains essential to consolidating operational gains and achieving lasting peace and security across the Northeast.” Goni explained. End The post Troops neutralise 15 terrorists in Borno appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nicolas Jackson double sees Aston Villa end Manchester City’s perfect start
item.description: Manchester City added a loss in the Premier League to one to the Premier League, as their perfect record this season vanished without an independent commission in sight. Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland. City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca. Continue reading...

item.title: Thousands March In France Against Far-Right Party Congress
item.description: Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the French city of Orléans Saturday against a congress by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party there, AFP journalists saw. The protest — held on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living after ones a week ago that devolved into street violence — criticised both Le Pen and centrist President Emmanuel Macron. France’s President Emmanuel Macron meets with elected officials at the town hall following a shooting in Trappes, near Paris, on October 23, 2026. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled, while carrying placards that read “The Youth say ‘screw you’ to the National Rally” and “Hotter than fascists”. The two-day RN congress in Orleans was the first big party campaign rally by Le Pen, whom surveys put as the leading candidate to succeed Macron in presidential elections in six months. AFP The post Thousands March In France Against Far-Right Party Congress appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Macron condemns racist terrorist attack in Paris suburb
item.description: Adding to the tensions, France is reeling from a shooting that authorities are investigating as a potentially racist and Islamophobic terrorist attack. One person was killed and five others wounded in the Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière, including a 12-year-old girl who was shot eight times. Police arrested the suspected gunman, and investigators reportedly found three gas cylinders rigged to a timer in his apartment, as well as a submachine gun in his car. The French president has condemned the attack, while the mayor of Saint-Denis has denounced the impact of hate speech.

item.title: Paris: Protest starts at Porte d'Italie, after last-minute change to the route
item.description: France is bracing for another day of cost-of-living protests, with extra police deployed nationwide to prevent a repeat of the violence that followed last Saturday’s demonstrations. In Lyon, where protests have been banned, police used tear gas to disperse around 150 people who had gathered to demonstrate. Government figures put last weekend’s turnout at more than half a million, and similarly large crowds could take to the streets again today. The movement grew out of high school students’ protests over poor conditions and a lack of resources, and cities across the country have stepped up security. In Paris, the Louvre, Orsay and Picasso museums are closed, while many luxury boutiques have also shut their doors and boarded up their windows following last weekend’s looting. France 24 Journalist Elitsa Gadeva reports the latest.

item.title: The Road To 2027 Runs Through Kaduna, But The North Is Not A Number
item.description: President Bola Tinubu will formally open his re-election campaign in Kaduna on Saturday. The location is deliberate, the arithmetic is formidable, and the message is unmistakable: the All Progressives Congress intends to win the 2027 election by rebuilding a northern coalition around the President. The three northern geopolitical zones contain 56.01 million of Nigeria’s 103.43 million registered voters; 54.2 per cent of the national register. The North-West alone has 25.08 million, making it the country’s largest electoral bloc. APC campaign officials are consequently talking about northern consensus and setting a national target of approximately 40 million votes. But registered voters are not actual votes, political endorsements are not public opinion, and the North is not a single electoral personality. That is the political signal this week. Why Kaduna matters Kaduna is in the North-West region. Kaduna is an appropriate starting point because it captures both the opportunity and the danger confronting Tinubu. It is a major political centre in the North-West, but it is not naturally secure territory for the President. Tinubu lost Kaduna to Atiku Abubakar in 2023. The state also embodies several issues that could determine northern voting behaviour: insecurity, rural poverty, food prices, religious sensitivity and the relationship between elite political agreements and popular sentiment. By beginning there, the APC is signalling that it will not concede the region to Atiku merely because he is a northern Muslim. It is relying on Vice-President Kashim Shettima, governors, ministers, traditional relationships and a greatly expanded party structure to offset Atiku’s regional appeal. That structure matters. The APC now enjoys an extraordinary advantage in the number of governors, lawmakers and local political networks under its control. Governors influence campaign financing, mobilisation and the organisation required to convert public sympathy into votes. The party’s challenge is that political machinery can mobilise supporters, but it cannot permanently insulate an incumbent from lived economic experience. The contest between structure and hardship The APC’s campaign argument will be that the most painful period of reform has passed. Inflation has moderated, foreign reserves have improved, economic growth has strengthened, and the Central Bank has begun adjusting interest rates. The administration will argue that removing the petrol subsidy and reforming the foreign-exchange market prevented a deeper fiscal crisis. The opposition’s reply is more immediate: food, transport, energy and business costs remain painfully high. That explains the political significance of the National Economic Council’s newly approved 90-day action plan.
